## [The catalog — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/catalogo.html)

Find a product in Zentrix Sales by name, code or barcode, use the scanner and filters, choose which price list you see and share a product on WhatsApp.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### The catalog

Everything your company sells, with its price, its weight and how much is left. You open it from the «Catálogo» (Catalog) tab at the bottom.

### Finding a product

Each product with its price, pack size, code, weight and how many units are left.

Type in the «Buscar producto o código…» (Search product or code…) field. The app searches three things at once:

- The product name.

- The company’s code (for example CM0521).

- The barcode on the package.

You don’t need to type the full name or use accents. Two or three letters are enough to filter.

### The scanner

Inside the same field, on the right, is the scanner icon. Tap it, point the camera at the barcode and you’re done: the code is typed into the search box for you and the list is filtered.

It’s handy standing in front of the shelf, when the customer shows you a package and you don’t know what it’s called in the system.

### If you search for something and it doesn’t show up

The app tells you whether that product is carried but can’t be sold today, and why:

- Agotado (Out of stock) — bring it on your next visit.

- Sin precio (No price) — the office sorts that out. Don’t promise a date.

Don’t tell the customer we don’t carry it without checking that first.

### Filters

The button to the right of the search box opens the filter sheet:

- Departamento (Department) and Categoría (Category) — they’re also chips above the list («Todo» (All), «SUPERMERCADO»…).

- Precio (Price) — a range, based on the price you see on the card.

- «Solo con oferta» (On sale only) — leaves only what has a reduced price.

- «Mostrar agotados» (Show out of stock) — off by default. Turn it on if you want to see them anyway.

- Orden (Sort) — how the list is arranged.

### When you have more than one price list

If you work with two or more price lists at this company, a button appears between the scanner and the filters. Tapping it opens «Con qué tarifa ves los precios» (Which price list you see prices with).

- By default it’s set to «Todas» (All): the app shows the lowest price across all your price lists, with the word «desde» (from) in front. The catalog doesn’t know which customer you’re visiting, so there’s no single price: the only honest figure is the floor.

- If you pick a price list, the «desde» disappears and you see that price list’s price, plain. The button reminds you which one is selected.

Your choice is saved per company. If you switch companies, that company has its own setting.

### The product page

Tap any product in the list to open its page: the photo, the price (struck through if it’s on sale, with the discount percentage), the equivalent in bolívars, the weight, how many units are available and the code — tap it to copy it, so you can read it out to the office over the phone. Further down is «Tus tarifas en esta empresa» (Your price lists at this company), with what it costs on each one.

### Sending the product to a customer on WhatsApp

At the top right of the product page is the share button. It builds a message with the name, the code, the price (and its equivalent in bolívars) and whether there’s stock for delivery.

Heads up
The customer gets a single price: the one you’re seeing at the top of the screen. The list of all your price lists isn’t sent, on purpose. Sending all four shows them the price someone else gets, and that message stays saved on their phone.

### «Sin precio» and «Falta bajar la tarifa»

They’re two different things, and they’re fixed differently:

What it says What’s happening What to do

«Sin precio» (No price) That product has no price set on any of your price lists. It’s for the office. Let them know and don’t promise a date.

«Falta bajar la tarifa» (Price list not downloaded yet) This company’s price list hasn’t been downloaded to your phone yet. Get online for a moment and sync. It fixes itself.


---

## [New customers and corrections — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/clientes.html)

How to propose a new customer from Zentrix Sales and suggest a correction to one you already have: the steps, the documents and where your request stands.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### New customers and corrections

You don’t create customers: you propose them. Someone at the office reviews and decides.

Don’t get this wrong
Neither a new customer request nor a correction changes the customer on its own. A person at the office reviews it. Don’t promise the customer it’s done: tell them you sent it.

All of this lives in «Mis solicitudes de cliente» (My customer requests), one of the buttons on the Home screen. That’s where the customers you asked to add and the corrections you proposed come together.

### Requesting a new customer

The «Cliente nuevo» (New customer) button, at the top of that screen. There are three steps.

- «¿Ya existe este cliente?» (Does this customer already exist?) Search by RIF (tax ID) or name. It’s required and it comes first: many stores are already in the system under another name, and adding them again creates a duplicate customer. If the one you’re looking for appears, the app tells you what to do with it. If it really isn’t there, tap «Ninguno es: dar de alta uno nuevo» (None of these: add a new one).

- «Datos del cliente» (Customer details) Document type, RIF or ID number, name, phone, email (required), address and an optional note for the office. The app checks the RIF as you type and warns you if the number doesn’t add up. Then, «Seguir con los recaudos» (Continue to documents).

- «Recaudos» (Documents) The store’s paperwork. When you have it, «Mandar a la oficina» (Send to the office).

Heads up
Adding a customer needs signal to START. It’s not a whim: that first search is what prevents the duplicate customer, and it can’t be done without internet.

From then on, everything works without signal: filling in the details, capturing the documents and sending it. If you don’t have signal when you send it, it stays saved and goes out by itself.

### The required documents

For each document you have two options:

- «Sacarle una foto» (Take a photo) — the app turns it into a PDF by itself. That’s the usual way: the ID card, the RIF, the articles of incorporation.

- «Cargar un PDF del teléfono» (Upload a PDF from the phone) — the one the customer already sent you on WhatsApp or by email. No need to print it just to photograph it again.

Each line says «Obligatorio» (Required) or «Opcional» (Optional), and once you’ve captured it, it says «Listo» (Done) with the file size.

«Obligatorio» warns, it doesn’t block
If you tap «Mandar a la oficina» and one is missing, a notice appears that lists them and gives you two options: «Tomar los que faltan» (Capture the missing ones) or «Mandar igual» (Send anyway). Some stores really don’t have one of those documents. Nothing is sent until you confirm.

### Correcting a customer you already have

This does not go through «Cliente nuevo». Open the customer page — from Mis clientes (My customers) or from the route — and tap «Sugerir una corrección» (Suggest a correction).

- Change only what’s wrong. Under each field you see «Hoy dice: …» (Currently says: …), which is what the office has on file today.

- If a field says «No bajamos este dato» (We didn’t download this data), it means your phone doesn’t have it: it doesn’t mean it’s empty.

- You can add «Por qué» (Why) — “moved to the corner,” “changed owners.” It helps the reviewer.

- Finish with «Enviar para que la revisen» (Send for review).

Corrections work fully without signal. If there’s no internet, it stays saved on the phone and goes out by itself.

### Where your request can end up

What the chip says What it means

Por enviar (To send) It’s on your phone, waiting for signal. It goes out by itself.

No se pudo enviar (Couldn’t be sent) It tried several times and couldn’t. Open it and take a look.

Esperando que la revisen (Waiting for review) It has reached the office. A person still needs to look at it. It doesn’t mean approved.

Te la devolvieron (Sent back to you) You need to correct something. Open it: it says what.

Cliente creado (Customer created) / Aprobada (Approved) Done. The request created the customer; the correction has been applied.

Rechazada (Rejected) It didn’t go through. The reason is inside.

Tap any card to open it and see what you proposed, the documents you sent and the reason, if there is one.


---

## [Collecting from a customer — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/cobrar.html)

How to record a payment in Zentrix Sales: bank, amount, reference and receipt, how to apply it to invoices and how to track the status of your request.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Collecting from a customer

When a customer pays you, you record it in the app. That’s called a payment request: you enter what you received and Finance reviews it later.

Don’t get this wrong
«Enviada» (Sent) doesn’t mean «Aprobada» (Approved). When you tap «Enviar solicitud» (Send request), the payment reaches Finance and waits there. Someone checks it against the bank, and only then is it deducted from the customer’s debt.

Tell the customer: “I’ve reported it, Finance is reviewing it.” Don’t tell them their invoice is paid, because it isn’t yet.

### Where to start

There are five ways in, and they all lead to the same screen, «Nueva solicitud» (New request):

- The «Cobrar» (Collect) button on the Home screen.

- The «Cobrarle» (Collect from them) button on the customer page. You go in with the customer already filled in, without searching the list.

- The «Cobrarle» button on the «¡Visita enviada!» (Visit sent!) screen, below «Ir al inicio» (Go to Home). It’s for the customer whose visit you just closed: if they paid you right there, you record it without going to look for them.

- The «Cobranza» (Collections) tab at the bottom, «Pagos» (Payments) sub-tab, and the + button to the right of the search box.

- An invoice’s «Subir pago» (Upload payment) button, in [Collections › Invoices](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/facturas.html). That way you go in with the customer already filled in.

### The walkthrough

- Who you’re collecting from If you came in through «Cobrar» or the +, the app asks you first. Search for the customer by name or RIF (tax ID). Right at the top you’ll see their name and RIF, so you can confirm it’s the right one.

- «Cómo te pagaron» (How you were paid) Tap the field and a list opens with the banks and cash accounts. Bolívar banks come first and dollar ones after. There’s a search box at the top: type part of the bank’s name and the list gets shorter.

- «Monto que recibiste» (Amount you received) Enter what the customer gave you, in the currency of the bank you picked. Below it, the app shows you the day’s exchange rate so you know what it’s worth.

- «Referencia / Nº depósito» (Reference / Deposit no.) It’s required — it has an asterisk. It’s the number Finance uses to find the payment at the bank. You can’t send without it.

- The receipt Tap «Adjuntar Comprobantes» (Attach receipts) and take the photo, or choose the screenshot the customer sent you. It’s the proof of payment.

- Additional photos If there was more than one transfer, tap «Agregar» (Add) under «Fotos adicionales» (Additional photos). You can add up to three. They go to the request’s conversation, where Finance sees them.

- Which invoices it applies to Further down is «Facturas pendientes» (Open invoices). Check the invoices that payment settles and split the amount among them. At the end, the app shows you «Total asignado» (Total allocated) and «Restante» (Remaining).

### If you leave the amount blank, the app fills it in

On an invoice with withholding (see below), you don’t need to fill in «Monto que recibiste» first. If you leave it blank and tap «Cobrar el total» (Collect the total) or «Retiene: cobrar» (Withholds: collect), the app enters that amount for you. From then on, as long as the amount is the one it entered, it’s always the sum of everything you allocated across the invoices: you check another one, uncheck one, correct an invoice’s amount, and the amount received adds itself up again. That way what you received and what you allocated can’t say different things.

- If the bank is in bolívars, the sum is converted to bolívars at the rate you see on the form.

- If you typed the amount yourself, the app doesn’t touch it. You read it off the receipt, and that takes precedence.

- If you later switch to a bank in another currency, the amount you had typed is cleared and the app tells you — «Cambiaste a un diario en bolívares: escribe de nuevo el monto que recibiste.» (“You switched to a bolívar journal: enter the amount you received again.”) — because that number was in the other currency.

- The «Auto» button splits what you received across the invoices in the usual order, keeps whatever you already typed on an invoice and unchecks the ones that end up with nothing.

The same screen, further down: the receipts, the additional photos and the open invoices.

Heads up
If you see «Este cliente ya tiene 3 solicitudes sin aprobar» (“This customer already has 3 unapproved requests”) at the top, check before you send. It may be the same deposit you already entered.

### When the customer withholds VAT

Some customers withhold VAT: they pay you less than the invoice says and give you a withholding certificate. Until that document reaches the office, the invoice keeps showing the full balance.

On those invoices, the app no longer fills in the amount on its own. The «Monto a pagar» (Amount to pay) field opens empty, with the math above it so you can follow it with your finger — invoice balance, minus the withholding still to apply, equals the expected balance — and two buttons below:

If you tap It’s because

Cobrar el total (Collect the total) The customer paid the full invoice and didn’t withhold anything.

Retiene: cobrar (Withholds: collect) The customer withheld the VAT and gave you the certificate. This button already has the withholding subtracted.

The button doesn’t lock you in: if they paid you a different amount, type it by hand. And if you haven’t filled in «Monto que recibiste» yet, the button fills it with its figure — you don’t have to scroll up to type it.

Why it asks you
Neither answer is always right. The app used to pick one, and only half of January’s withholdings ended up being applied — in other words, it guessed wrong one time in two, and “if you didn’t notice, a balance was left over.”

The person who knows whether the customer withheld is you, with the certificate in your hand.

### Any overpayment stays as customer credit

If you received more than you applied to the invoices, the app tells you before you send, on the «Restante» (Remaining) line:

Los $19,00 que sobran no van contra ninguna factura: le quedan al cliente a favor para su próxima compra. (“The extra $19.00 doesn’t go against any invoice: it stays as credit for the customer’s next purchase.”)
That money isn’t lost. Tell the customer right then, when it’s useful.

### You can collect without signal

If there’s no internet, the button at the bottom changes to «Guardar cobranza sin señal» (Save collection offline). The request is saved on your phone, photo and all, and goes out by itself when the network comes back. Don’t enter it again.

Meanwhile you’ll see it in Cobranza › Pagos (Collections › Payments) as «Por enviar» (To send).

### Tracking your request

All your collections are in Cobranza › Pagos (Collections › Payments). Each one shows its status on the right:

It says What’s happening

Por enviar (To send) It’s on your phone. It goes out by itself when there’s signal.

No se pudo enviar (Couldn’t be sent) It was tried several times and didn’t go out. Let your analyst know.

Enviada (Sent) It reached the office. It’s waiting for Finance to review it.

Devuelta (Returned) Finance found something to correct. It’s back in your hands.

Aprobada (Approved) Done. Now it has been deducted from the customer’s debt.

Cancelada (Canceled) The office voided it. It can’t be touched.

The chips at the top let you filter: «Todas» · «En revisión» · «Devueltas» · «Canceladas» · «Aprobadas» (All · Under review · Returned · Canceled · Approved).

### Correcting a request

You can correct a request that is «Enviada» (Sent) or «Devuelta» (Returned). Tap the request to open it and use «Corregir y reenviar» (Correct and resend). On a returned one, the button also appears in the list, because it’s something you have pending.

Heads up
An «Aprobada» or «Cancelada» request can’t be corrected: it’s already an accounting entry at the office.

And correcting requires signal. It isn’t saved for later, because in the meantime the analyst may have picked it up.

You don’t re-upload the receipt
When you correct, you’ll see the receipt you already sent. If you don’t attach a new one, that one is kept. Only take a new photo if the problem was the receipt.


---

## [Talking to the office — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/conversacion.html)

How to talk to the office from Zentrix Sales: the conversation on an order, invoice, collection or customer, with internal notes, mentions and attachments.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Talking to the office

Every order, every invoice, every collection and every customer has its own conversation with the office. It isn’t a separate chat: it’s attached to the document you’re talking about.

The internal note is amber with a padlock; your message is in the app’s color: blue since 5.3.0 (in the screenshot, the purple of the previous design).

### Where to find it

Look for the «Conversación» (Conversation) button in the details of:

- an order, in [Activity](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html);

- an invoice, in [Cobranza › Facturas (Collections › Invoices)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/facturas.html);

- a collection request, in [Cobranza › Pagos (Collections › Payments)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/cobrar.html);

- a customer, on their customer page.

At the top of the conversation there’s always the document number, so you know what you’re talking about.

Heads up
An order or a collection that’s still on your phone has no conversation: it doesn’t exist at the office yet. The button tells you so instead of opening an empty screen. Get online and it goes out by itself.

### Message or internal note

At the bottom, to the left of the text field, there’s a switch. These are two different things:

What it is Who sees it

Message Everyone following the document at the office.

Internal note 🔒 Only you and anyone you mention. It shows in amber with a padlock.

The amber notes nobody wrote — «Orden de venta creado» (Sales order created) — are added by the system on its own, to keep the document’s history.

### Mentioning someone

The @ button opens the list of people you can mention. The person you mention gets an alert, even if it’s an internal note.

That’s what you use when you need someone in particular: don’t just write it and hope whoever passes by reads it.

### Sending a photo or a PDF

The paper clip attaches files. You can send a photo taken on the spot or build a PDF by photographing pages.

Don’t get this wrong
A message’s text is saved and goes out by itself when you get a signal. An attachment isn’t. To send a photo or a PDF you need internet at that moment: if there isn’t any, the app tells you and nothing is queued.

If you’re without signal and the attachment matters, send the text now and the photo when you have data.

### When someone writes to you

It arrives as an alert on the bell and as a phone notification. Tapping it opens that document’s conversation, not a generic inbox.

And if you already have it open, the new message appears by itself: no need to leave and come back. The screen doesn’t jump while you’re scrolling up to read.

### Without signal

The conversation is saved on the phone and you can read it again without internet, stamped with when it was saved. If it was never downloaded, the app tells you — an empty conversation would read as “nobody wrote to you,” and that would be a lie.

What you write without signal stays «Por enviar» (To send) and goes out by itself. Two messages are two messages: resending them doesn’t duplicate them.


---

## [Quick answers — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/dudas.html)

The most common Zentrix Sales questions in a sentence or two: the PIN, location permission, prices that change, alerts, updates and the sync dot.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Quick answers

The most common questions, in a sentence or two.

### The app closed in the middle of a visit. Did I lose the order?

No. It was saved half-built and you’ll find it in [Activity › Orders › «Abiertos» (Open)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#abiertos); its stop says «En curso» (In progress). Open it and pick up where you left off.

### Why does it ask me for a PIN?

So that nobody who picks up your unlocked phone can see prices, debts and customers. It’s requested when you open the app and after 15 minutes without touching anything.

### How do I change the PIN?

In Perfil › Cuenta › «Cambiar PIN» (Profile › Account › Change PIN). It asks for the current one first. If you don’t remember it, sign out and sign in with your password.

### Why does it need location permission to take an order?

Because a visit has to be able to say where it happened. What’s needed is granting the permission, not a GPS fix: you’ll still be able to sell inside a warehouse.

### I said “Don’t allow” and now it won’t ask again.

Android doesn’t ask a third time. Tap «Abrir los ajustes» (Open settings) in the notice and grant the permission there; when you come back, the notice disappears by itself.

### Why did the price change when the order reached the office?

Prices are the ones in effect the day the order enters the system, not the day you took it. The app tells you which product changed: let the customer know before the invoice reaches them.

### It says the customer is over their credit limit. Do I send the order?

Yes. The app never stops an order because of credit: the warning is there so you request approval right away, with the «Pedir autorización» (Request approval) button, while the customer is in front of you. At the office the order stays «Retenido» (On hold) until it’s approved. It’s explained in [the visit](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/visita.html#limite-de-credito).

### A screen came up asking me to update.

The office can tell you about a new version without waiting for the app store to offer it. There are two kinds, and they aren’t the same:

- A notice you can close. Update when you can and keep working. If the office withdraws it, the notice disappears by itself the next time the app checks in with the office; if you’re in a hurry, pull down on the Home screen to refresh.

- A screen that won’t let you through. That version no longer works with the office’s system; you have to update to continue.

What you’ve already entered is NOT lost, not even with that screen showing. Any orders and collections you haven’t sent yet go out by themselves in the background, as always. Don’t enter them again and don’t uninstall the app.

The button takes you to the right app store for your phone. If it can’t open it, the app tells you: search for “Zentrix Sales” by hand.

### I’m not getting alerts.

It’s almost always the phone being on silent. If that’s it, the Home screen tells you, with a button to fix it. Also check that Zentrix Sales is allowed to show notifications.

### I switched companies and the catalog has no prices.

That company’s price list hasn’t been downloaded yet. Get online for a moment and tap «Sincronizar ahora» (Sync now): it fixes itself.

### Another rep uses this same phone. Do our things get mixed up?

No. Each person has their own customers, orders and pending items saved, kept apart by email. Signing out doesn’t delete anything of yours: when you sign back in, everything is just as you left it.

### How do I remove an old account from the sign-in list?

On the sign-in screen, «Manejar cuentas» (Manage accounts). There you can remove it from the list (its data stays saved) or delete it completely. First check how many unsent items it has.

### The dot is amber all day. Is something wrong?

No. Amber means “some of your items are waiting” or “there’s no signal,” and on the road that’s normal. Only worry if it’s red. It’s explained in [Working offline](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/sin-internet.html#el-punto).

### The camera won’t open and I can’t take the visit photo.

The photo isn’t required: you can close the visit without it. The order, the stock count and the signature are saved anyway.

### I sent a collection and it says «Enviada». Has it been collected?

No. «Enviada» (Sent) means it reached the office and someone in Finance is going to approve it. Aprobada (Approved) is a different status.

### Something doesn’t add up?

If a number doesn’t add up or something doesn’t behave the way this documentation says, don’t guess: note the customer, the time and what you expected to see, and pass it on. A report with those three details gets fixed; one that says “it doesn’t work” doesn’t.

In the app you have Perfil › Acerca de › «Reportar un problema» (Profile › About › Report a problem). Describe what happened and send it: the report travels with the exact version, the phone model and the last steps you took — which is exactly what someone has to guess when the same problem arrives over WhatsApp.

Perfil › Acerca de › Soporte (Profile › About › Support) has help and contact details. You can also write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company), which is also the mailbox for any question about your personal data.

That form doesn’t reply to you
It’s for fixing the app, and nobody will answer you through it. If you need someone to sort something out for you today, write to support.

Zentrix Sales support — email, phone and WhatsApp — is on [the support page](https://zentrix.company/en/support/#sales).


---

## [Signing in and syncing — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/entrar.html)

How to sign in to Zentrix Sales the first time with your company domain, your email and an optional PIN, and why you should sync before heading out.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Signing in and syncing

You only do this once. After that, the app recognizes you and you go straight in.

### Signing in the first time

- The domain It’s the address of your company’s system, for example ventas.tuempresa.com. Type it in full, without https:// or slashes: the app fills that in. The office gives it to you. Before saving it, the app checks that the server responds; if it doesn’t, it tells you and saves nothing.

- Your email and password The same ones you use to sign in to your company’s system.

- The PIN, if you want one Four digits. It stops anyone who picks up your unlocked phone from opening Zentrix Sales and seeing your customers’ prices, debts and addresses. You can tap «Ahora no» (Not now) and go in anyway — the app won’t ask again, and you can turn it on whenever you like in Perfil › Cuenta (Profile › Account).

From then on
You never type your email or the domain again: the app saves your account. If you were already using the app before 5.3.0, you don’t have to type anything: your domain is already saved. If you set a PIN, the app asks for it after 15 minutes of not using it.

### Sync before you head out

With a good signal, open the app and wait for the little dot in the top corner to turn green. To speed it up, tap it and then «Sincronizar ahora» (Sync now).

Tap the dot and this panel opens. It tells you the status in plain words and how old each piece of data is.

That downloads to your phone your customer list, prices, the catalog, available stock, exchange rates and what customers owe you. With that, you can work the whole day even if you lose signal.

The panel shows you, line by line, how old each piece of data is and how much you still have to send. The first time you open the app each day, it also tells you whether «Ya puedes salir a la calle» (“You’re ready to head out”) and, if something essential is missing, what it is.

Heads up
If you head out without syncing, the app works just the same — but with yesterday’s prices and balances. Two minutes in the morning save you an argument with a customer.

### The PIN

It’s optional, and you’re asked only once per account: if you answered «Ahora no» (Not now), the app won’t insist again — not that day, and not every time you sign out.

Once the PIN is set, it’s requested every time 15 minutes go by without you touching anything. You turn it on or change it in Perfil › Cuenta, and to change it the app asks for the current one first.

There’s no “forgot my PIN”, and that’s on purpose: it would be a back door for anyone holding your phone. If you don’t remember it, sign out and sign in again with your password.

It’s worth setting
Behind the PIN are each customer’s prices, how much they owe you and where their stores are. A phone lost with the session open and no PIN hands all of that over.

### If two reps share the phone

Nothing gets mixed up. Each person has their own customers, orders and pending items saved, kept apart by email. Signing out doesn’t delete anything of yours: when you sign back in, everything is just as you left it.

On the sign-in screen, «Manejar cuentas» (Manage accounts) lets you remove an account from the list (its data stays saved) or delete it completely. First check how many unsent items it has.

## [Invoices and what’s owed — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/facturas.html)

How to read customer balances in Zentrix Sales: owed, overdue and under review, the invoice cards, colored tags, payment promises and invoice currency.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Invoices and what customers owe

All your customers’ debt is in one place: the «Cobranza» (Collections) tab at the bottom, «Facturas» (Invoices) sub-tab.

### The header: three numbers

The header with the three numbers, and the cards with «CÓBRALE HOY» (COLLECT TODAY).

- TE DEBEN (OWED TO YOU) — everything your customers haven’t paid.

- VENCIDO (OVERDUE) — of that, what’s already past its due date.

- EN REVISIÓN (UNDER REVIEW) — what you’ve already collected and Finance hasn’t approved yet.

All three are in dollars. That’s on purpose: they add up invoices in bolívars and in dollars, and those can only be compared in a single currency.

Below, it says how many invoices there are and how old the data is. Tap «Ver detalle» (See details) to read the explanatory notes. At the top are the «Todas» · «Vencidas» · «Por vencer» (All · Overdue · Coming due) chips and the search box, where you can type the customer, the RIF (tax ID) or the invoice number.

Don’t get this wrong
What’s «EN REVISIÓN» you’ve already collected from the customer. It’s money on its way, waiting for approval. Don’t ask them for it again.

That amount is not deducted from «TE DEBEN»: that’s why the two numbers sit side by side.

### Why the card shows two numbers

The big number says «CÓBRALE HOY» (COLLECT TODAY). That’s the one you ask the customer for.

On the right, in small print, it says «de $237,66» (of $237.66). That’s the invoice’s full balance, the one printed on paper.

The two differ when there’s something that no longer needs to be collected:

- VAT withholding — the customer withheld part of it and pays it directly to SENIAT (the tax authority). They don’t give you that part.

- Your collections awaiting approval — you’ve already collected something on that invoice and Finance hasn’t approved it yet. It shows up as a pill: «− $0,12 · en revisión» (− $0.12 · under review).

Below the number, the app shows you the full subtraction so you can follow it with your finger.

Heads up
If «CÓBRALE HOY» is zero and grayed out, you’ve already collected that invoice and it’s waiting for approval. Don’t collect from the customer again.

### How long it’s been overdue

At the top right of the card, in red, it says «Vencida hace 27 días» (Overdue 27 days) or «Vencida hace un mes» (Overdue a month). That’s what tells you which of seven invoices to collect first.

If the invoice isn’t due yet, it says when it’s due and isn’t shown in red.

### The colored tags

Some invoices carry tags from the office, each with its own color: «DEUDA PARCIAL» (PARTIAL DEBT), «LEGAL», «CASO IRREGULAR» (IRREGULAR CASE)… They’re the same ones the office uses, in the same color, so you recognize them at a glance. You can add them too.

### The card’s three buttons

At the bottom left are three round buttons. Press and hold one to see its name:

- Etiquetas (Tags) — you tag the invoice so the office sees it.

- Compromiso (Promise) — you note when the customer promised to pay.

- Subir pago (Upload payment) — the most used: it opens [the collection screen](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/cobrar.html) with that invoice already checked.

And on the right, «Ver factura →» (View invoice →) opens the full details, with the breakdown and the conversation with the office.

### The payment promise

It’s a promise from the customer that you write down: «¿Cuándo prometió pagar?» (When did they promise to pay?) and, if you like, how much. If you don’t enter an amount, only the date is recorded.

The card then says «Prometió pagar el 30/09» (Promised to pay on 09/30), and on that day the app reminds you to go collect. It’s also saved without signal and goes out by itself.

Heads up
You can’t promise more than the invoice owes, or set a date that has already passed. The app tells you when you save.

### The invoice currency and «de referencia»

Each invoice is shown in the currency it was issued in. If the invoice is in bolívars, the big number is in bolívars: it’s the same one the customer has on their paper and the same one Accounts will demand.

Below it you may see the same amount in the other currency with the words «de referencia» (for reference). That means: it’s just to help you get your bearings, not what you collect. It’s calculated at the rate the invoice was issued with, which on an old invoice isn’t today’s rate.

Don’t get this wrong
Always read the customer the big number, the one in their invoice’s currency. The one that says «de referencia» isn’t what you collect.


---

## [Zentrix Sales documentation — For field reps](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/)

The Zentrix Sales documentation for field reps, screen by screen: your route, the visit, orders, collections, invoices and working without a signal or internet.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### The Zentrix Sales rep documentation

What’s new in version 5.3.0. The app now carries the Zentrix Sales brand.

- A new look: an icon with the Zentrix “z”, a light theme by default (the dark one is still in Perfil (Profile)), the Inter typeface and Zentrix blue on buttons and messages. If you had already picked a theme, it stays.

- When you sign in, you type your company’s full domain. See [Signing in and syncing](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/entrar.html#entrar).

- Perfil › Acerca de (Profile › About) has the website, Soporte (Support) and the privacy policy. For questions about your personal data, write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company).

- The orders, payments and data saved on your phone stay as they are, and you don’t have to sign in again.

Some screenshots in this documentation still show the previous design, but the steps are the same.

How to use the app on the road, screen by screen. It’s written to be read on your phone, in whatever order you like.

### What you can’t forget

If you read nothing else today, read this. It’s five sentences, and each one saves you an argument with a customer.

Don’t get this wrong
«Enviada» (Sent) is not «Aprobada» (Approved). When you record a payment, tell the customer you have reported it — not that their invoice is paid. Someone in Finance reviews it later, and until they approve it, that debt is still open.

Don’t get this wrong
The price you see is a quote, not the invoice. The office recalculates prices and taxes when it receives the order, using the ones in effect the day it arrives. If the number changes, the app lets you know.

Don’t get this wrong
Nothing you do gets lost. Everything is saved on your phone the moment you do it and goes out by itself as soon as you get a signal: orders, collections, visits and returns. Even if you close the app, your phone shuts off or you spend the whole day without internet.

And the two habits:

- Sync in the morning. Two minutes with a good signal and you can work all day, even if you lose internet later.

- Close each visit the same day. An open visit hasn’t reached anyone. You’ll find them in Actividad › Pedidos › «Abiertos» (Activity › Orders › Open).

### What Zentrix Sales does

With Zentrix Sales you run your whole day on the road from your phone: you arrive at the store, build the customer’s order, collect payment, record what they returned and leave proof that you were there. It replaces the notebook, the calculator and the call to the office to ask how much someone owes.

It’s built for the road, not the office. It works without internet.

### The five tabs at the bottom

Tab What it’s for

Inicio (Home) Your dashboard for the day. Exchange rates, what you’ve done so far today and the eight shortcuts.

Catálogo (Catalog) Everything you can sell, with prices and available stock.

Actividad (Activity) Your orders, your visits and your returns.

Cobranza (Collections) What customers owe you and the payments you’ve recorded.

Perfil (Profile) Your account, the color theme, permissions and the PIN.

### You propose, the office confirms

Orders, collections and new customers all go through someone who reviews them. That isn’t red tape: it’s what protects you when there’s a complaint. The record shows what you sent, when and with what numbers.

### The documentation, section by section

Each section is a short page. You can send someone the link to just one.

### Start here

## [Your Home screen — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/inicio.html)

The screen you’ll see most in Zentrix Sales: the greeting, alerts, your company, the day’s exchange rates, the Today block and the eight quick shortcuts.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Your Home screen

The screen you’ll see most. Here’s what’s on it, from top to bottom.

The bottom half of the Home screen: exchange rates, the «Hoy» (Today) block and the shortcuts.

### From top to bottom

What it is What it’s for

The greeting Your name. Next to it, the bell for alerts and the sync dot.

Alerts They only show up when something needs fixing: the phone is on silent, a permission is missing. If nothing’s wrong, nothing shows.

Your company The logo, the name and the RIF (tax ID). If you work for several companies, you switch here.

Exchange rates Dollar, euro and the Central Bank rate. Tap them to open the full screen with the calculator and the history.

«Hoy» (Today) Closed visits, orders and the day’s amount. Tap it to go to Mi desempeño (My performance), with your target for the month.

The eight buttons The shortcuts. Each one shows a figure underneath.

An empty line isn’t a fault
If a piece of data hasn’t been downloaded, that line isn’t drawn. The app would rather say nothing than make up a number.

### The eight shortcuts

They are Crear pedido (Create order), Ruta de hoy (Today’s route), Cobrar (Collect), Mis clientes (My customers), Promociones (Promotions), Calendario (Calendar), Solicitudes de cliente (Customer requests) and Sin ubicación (No location).

The two filled in blue are the ones you’ll use every day: Crear pedido and Ruta de hoy.

Each button shows its own figure underneath — «40 clientes» (40 customers), «1 factura vence hoy» (1 invoice due today), «0 de 3 paradas» (0 of 3 stops) — so you know what’s waiting for you without opening it.

Each number says what it counts
The «Hoy» block says «Visitas cerradas» (Closed visits): it only counts the ones you’ve completed. In [Activity › Visits](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#visitas) the «Hoy» chip also counts the ones you still have open, so the number there can be higher. Both are right.

### Promociones (Promotions)

Your company’s current sales material: bundles, discounts and coupons. It’s your counter display — you open it in front of the customer to know what to offer them.

⚠️ It doesn’t apply anything to the order. The actual price still comes from the customer’s price list in the Order step; this screen is for information only. Without a signal it shows the last thing that was downloaded, always with the date.

### Stock adjustment

It isn’t on the Home screen: it opens with «Ajustar» (Adjust) on the bounced order, in Actividad › Pedidos (Activity › Orders). It’s for the order that bounced because there wasn’t as much stock as you ordered. It happens when you build the order without signal and, by the time it goes out, the warehouse no longer has those quantities.

Here you lower each line to what’s available and send it again. Prices don’t change — they’re the ones you quoted the customer — and it’s the same order, not a new one, so nothing gets duplicated. It’s explained in full in [Activity](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#rebotado-por-stock).

### Sin ubicación (No location)

The stores on your customer list that don’t have a pin on the map yet. The button tells you how many addresses are missing out of how many you have — «12 de 50 direcciones» (12 of 50 addresses) — because the pin belongs to each address: a customer with two branches counts twice.

The list is there for planning: you look at which ones they are, notice three are on the same avenue and add them to Thursday’s route.

Why you can’t set it from here
The pin can only be set standing at the store’s door, from the visit. Setting it from home by looking at a map is guessing which of the four corners it is, and your route and the proof that you were there both depend on that coordinate. That’s why this screen lists them but doesn’t let you set the pin.

### My performance

Tapping the «Hoy» block takes you to your performance: the month’s target with its traffic light, what you’ve sold so far, the weight and your streak.

Two things worth knowing about those numbers:

- They’re in dollars, even if the order was built in bolívars. It’s the only way to add up orders in two currencies and compare them.

- When the calculation came from this phone and not from the office, the screen says so. They may not match: the office closes the day in the early morning and sees all your devices; the phone only sees today and this device.


---

## [Today’s route — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/ruta.html)

How to plan and run your route in Zentrix Sales: assign customers to a day, sort your stops by distance, navigate there and take someone off the day.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Today’s route

You build the route yourself, on your phone. Nobody at the office imposes it on you, and it works without signal.

### Planning

Go in through «Ruta de hoy» (Today’s route) or «Calendario» (Calendar). If you don’t have anything yet, tap «Planificar ruta» (Plan route).

Down below are your «SIN PLANIFICAR» (UNPLANNED) customers. Tap «Asignar» (Assign) on the one you’re going to visit, pick the day and you’re done.

At the top you’ll see your coverage for the month: how many of your customers you’ve already visited.

### Running the route

Three stops, with each customer’s balance in view before you knock on the door.

The route shows your stops numbered, with the address, the RIF and — what matters — how much each one owes and whether anything is overdue.

- «Ordenar por cercanía» (Sort by distance) reorders them based on where you’re standing.

- «Navegar» (Navigate) opens your maps app to drive there.

- Tap a stop to start the visit.

- With the «⋮» button you can remove it from the day or open it in Maps.

- Press and hold, then drag to change the order by hand.

How old is what you’re seeing
Below the list, the route tells you when your customer list was downloaded: «guardados el 18/09 a las 07:12» (“saved on 09/18 at 07:12”). It’s not an error — it’s so you know how old the balance is before you tell the customer.

### Taking someone off the day

Swipe the card or use the «⋮» button › «Quitar de la ruta de hoy» (Remove from today’s route).

It’s just for today: they’re still your customer. Taking someone off your customer list is the office’s call; it can’t be done from here.

If you already checked in
The half-built order isn’t deleted: you’ll still find it in [Activity › Orders › «Abiertos» (Open)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#abiertos). What disappears from view is the route card, not the work.


---

## [Working offline — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/sin-internet.html)

Nothing gets lost in Zentrix Sales without signal: what each color of the sync dot means, how the panel works and what to do if an item couldn’t be sent.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### Working offline

This is the most important section of the documentation. Read it all the way through once and you won’t need it again.

Don’t get this wrong
Nothing gets lost. Everything you do on the road is saved on your phone the moment you do it and goes out by itself as soon as you get a signal: orders, collections, visits and returns. You don’t have to do anything.

### How it works

When you close a visit or record a payment, it’s written to your phone first. The app then takes care of sending it. Meanwhile:

- It keeps trying on its own every few minutes, even if you close the app.

- If your phone shuts off or runs out of battery, what was saved is still there when you turn it back on.

- If you send the same thing twice by mistake, the office doesn’t charge it twice. That’s covered.

You can work the whole day in airplane mode and wrap everything up once you reach a place with signal.

### The colored dot

In the top right corner of almost every screen there’s a dot. It shows the status of your outgoing items. Look at its color and shape:

What it looks like What it means

Green, solid Connected and everything sent. Nothing pending.

Amber Some of your items are waiting to go out, or there’s no signal. That’s normal on the road.

Red Something needs your decision. It won’t go out by itself: you have to open it.

Blue, with a bar «Estamos ejecutando mejoras» (“We’re rolling out improvements”). It’s not your phone: the office is updating the system. It comes back by itself in a few minutes.

Crossed-out ring No connection. Keep working as usual.

The dot pulses when you have something waiting, and an arc spins around it while it’s sending.

### The panel: tap the dot

The status in plain words, the button to send everything at once, and how old each piece of data is.

- At the top, the status: «Conectado · todo enviado» (“Connected · all sent”), «Sin conexión · 3 por enviar» (“Offline · 3 to send”), «1 envío necesita tu decisión» (“1 item needs your decision”).

- The «Sincronizar ahora» (Sync now) button, to send and download everything at once without waiting.

- «Por enviar» (To send) and «Necesitan tu decisión» (Need your decision), counted by type (orders, visits, collections…).

- «Para trabajar sin señal» (For working offline), with how many of your data sets are up to date. Expand it to see them line by line: customers, prices, catalog, available stock, exchange rates, customer debt…

Screens tell you how old the information is
When what you’re seeing comes from what’s saved on the phone rather than from the office, a small line appears at the bottom: «Facturas guardadas en el teléfono el 18/09 a las 07:12» (“Invoices saved on the phone on 09/18 at 07:12”).
That’s not an error. It’s there so you know how old the figure is before you tell the customer.

### Sync every morning

With good Wi-Fi or a good signal, open the app, tap the dot and hit «Sincronizar ahora» (Sync now). Wait until it says all your data is up to date.

That way you take the day’s prices, catalog, customers, their debts and exchange rates with you in the car. From then on you can work without signal and not be missing anything.

### If something says «No se pudo enviar»

Seeing amber or «por enviar» (to send) isn’t a problem: that goes out by itself. What you do need to look at is red, or an order that says «No se pudo enviar» (“Couldn’t be sent”). Do this, in order:

- Find a signal and wait a minute Most of the time it sorts itself out as soon as you get internet. Don’t touch anything yet.

- Open the panel and read the reason Tap the dot. Items that need your decision have a direct link («Ver pendientes en Pedidos», “See pending in Orders”). Open it: the app tells you why.

- Act on what it says «No salió de tu teléfono» (“It never left your phone”) or «Se rindió después de diez intentos» (“Gave up after ten attempts”): tap «Reintentar» (Retry) once you have signal. «Sin stock» (Out of stock): lower the quantity or discard it. «La oficina lo rechazó» (“The office rejected it”): sending it again as is won’t help; you need to rebuild it or let someone know.

- If it happens again, report it Give the order number or the customer and what the screen says. Nothing deletes itself: until you discard it, it stays there.

The panel also has «Reintentar los envíos que se rindieron» (Retry items that gave up), which puts them all back in the send queue at once.


---

## [The visit, step by step — Zentrix Sales documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/visita.html)

The eight steps of a Zentrix Sales visit: check-in, stock count, order, photos, returns, notes, signature and check-out, with what’s worth knowing.

Documentation for version 5.3.0

### The visit, step by step

A visit has eight steps: Check-in, Stock count, Order, Photos, Returns, Notes, Signature and Check-out. Here’s each one, with what you have to do and what’s worth knowing before you stand in front of the customer.

Don’t get this wrong
The visit doesn’t reach the office until you complete it in step 8. Until then it stays saved on your phone: it isn’t lost, but nobody sees it. Always close the visit before you leave the store.

### What a visit is

A visit is everything that happens at a store: that you arrived, what you counted on the shelf, what they bought, what they returned and what you noted down. The app brings it all together as a single piece of work.

At the top you always see which step you’re on: «Paso 3 de 8 — Pedido» (Step 3 of 8 — Order), with a bar of little dashes. You move forward with «Guardar y continuar →» (Save and continue →), the button at the bottom.

### How to start

There are two ways in, and both open the same thing:

- From the Home screen, tap «Crear pedido» (Create order). The «¿A quién vas a visitar?» (Who are you visiting?) sheet opens. Search by name, RIF (tax ID) or address and tap the customer. Next to each one you see what they owe you.

- From Ruta de hoy (Today’s route), tap the stop. The app already knows who you’re visiting.

If the customer has several branches, the app asks you «Qué dirección se visita» (Which address you’re visiting). Pick the right one: it determines where the order is delivered.

The location permission
To take an order, you need to have given the app location permission. If you haven’t, it asks for it and takes you to Settings.
The GPS doesn’t need to get a fix: the visit opens anyway, indoors or in a basement.

### Step 1 — Check-in

Step 1. The customer’s balance, the time and your location, all before you walk in.

This is saying “I’m here.” The screen shows you the customer, their billing address and what they owe you.

Two things fill themselves in, and you don’t have to wait for them:

- «Hora de llegada» (Arrival time) — the current time.

- «Tu ubicación» (Your location) — it says «Se toma sola — no tienes que esperarla» (“Captured automatically — you don’t have to wait for it”).

Tap «Confirmar llegada y continuar» (Confirm arrival and continue).

If the store doesn’t have its spot marked on the map yet, «Revisar la ubicación del negocio» (Check the store’s location) appears. Mark it while you’re standing at the door: it’s the best moment, and you won’t get another one.

Customer not buying today? Tap «El cliente no compra hoy — ir al cierre» (Customer isn’t buying today — go to check-out) and you jump straight to step 8. The visit is still recorded.

Heads up
You can check in without signal too. You’ll see «Llegada guardada en el teléfono — se envía cuando haya señal» (“Arrival saved on the phone — it will be sent when there’s signal”). Keep working as usual.

### Step 2 — Stock count

Here you count what the customer has on their shelf. It isn’t an order: it’s a snapshot of how well stocked they are.

Find the product and set the quantity with − and +, or tap the number to type it in directly.

Heads up
There’s no cap in this step: if the customer has 40 on the shelf, you enter 40, even if the warehouse has fewer. And products that don’t have a price loaded yet show up too — they’re on the shelf all the same.

### Step 3 — Order

Step 3. Available stock, the case pack size and the total at the bottom.

This is the heart of the visit: what the customer buys from you.

- Search by name or code in the bar at the top.

- Scan the barcode with the square button. If the code isn’t on your list, the app tells you.

- Tap the product image to open its full product page.

- When the product comes in cases, choose the pack size: «UND» (unit) or «CAJ24 · 24 uds» (case of 24 · 24 units). The price and weight update by themselves.

Under each product you see «Disponible: 77 uds» (Available: 77 units). That’s what you can sell right now from that warehouse, not what’s in storage. You can’t enter more than that.

At the bottom is the Total bar, with its equivalent in bolívars and the weight. Next to it are three buttons: build another order for the same customer, «Pedir autorización por WhatsApp» (Request approval on WhatsApp) and «Compartir presupuesto» (Share quote).

### Skipping to check-out

If you already have the order and you’re not going to take photos, accept a return, write notes or ask for a signature, you don’t need to go through those four empty steps. The total bar shows «Ir al cierre» (Go to check-out), which takes you straight to Check-out.

- It only appears if those steps are empty. If you’ve already taken a photo or counted a return, you continue the normal way.

- Nothing that matters gets skipped: the pre-send checks still run at check-out.

- Remembered something? From check-out, the back arrow takes you back, step by step, through the ones you skipped.

If the customer isn’t buying today, the shortcut is a different one: «El cliente no compra hoy — ir al cierre».

### When the order goes over the customer’s credit limit

At companies that control credit, if this order takes the customer over their limit, the app tells you in amber — on the total bar, at check-out and in the final confirmation — along with how far over it goes:

Con este pedido el cliente pasa su límite por $120,00 (12,00 %). Odoo lo va a retener hasta que lo aprueben: pide la autorización ya. (“With this order the customer goes over their limit by $120.00 (12.00%). Odoo will hold it until it’s approved: request approval now.”)
Next to it is «Pedir autorización» (Request approval), which drafts the message for the approver with the customer’s figures.

Credit figures are in dollars. On the customer page, under «Su cuenta» (Their account), you see them in order: Cupo de crédito (Credit limit), Usado (Used), Por facturar (To invoice — confirmed orders that haven’t been invoiced yet) and Disponible (Available). You can follow the math with your finger: limit minus used minus to invoice gives you available, and if it comes out negative it shows in red.

Don’t get this wrong
The warning doesn’t stop you. The order is sent anyway and reaches the office; there it stays [«Retenido» (On hold)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#estados) until it’s authorized. The warning is there so you request approval right away, with the customer in front of you, instead of finding out days later.

Without signal, it uses the figures saved on the phone and says so: «Cifras de crédito guardadas en el teléfono, sin confirmar con Odoo.» (“Credit figures saved on the phone, not confirmed with Odoo.”)

### Several orders in the same visit

A customer may buy things from you that ship separately — one without alcohol, one with sweets, one with groceries. That isn’t three visits: it’s one visit with three orders.

This visit’s orders, with the active one highlighted and its three-dot menu.

- Once you’ve added something, tap the another order button on the total bar. It only appears when the current order has items: it won’t let you open two blank documents.

- The chips appear at the top: «Pedido 1 · 3 productos» (Order 1 · 3 products), «Pedido 2 · 1 producto»… Tap one to switch orders. It’s the same catalog for all of them.

- The new order starts empty and with its own pack sizes: the case you chose for the rum doesn’t decide anything about the flour in the order next to it.

- The active order’s chip has a «⋮» with «Vaciar este pedido» (Empty this order) and «Quitar este pedido» (Remove this order). If it has products, the app asks you first.

Who decides what goes in each one
You do, with one exception: liquor (below). Other than that, the app doesn’t split anything by category or anything else on its own: the orders are whatever you build. And an empty order doesn’t travel — if you opened one and didn’t add anything, no blank document reaches the office.

### Liquor goes in its own order

Some companies don’t allow liquor to be mixed with other products in the same order. At those companies, if you add both together, the app splits the order in two when you leave the Order step: one with the liquor and one with the rest. It tells you like this:

Salen dos pedidos: esta empresa no permite mezclar licor con otros productos en un mismo pedido. (“Two orders will be sent: this company doesn’t allow liquor to be mixed with other products in the same order.”)

- They’re two documents at the office, each with its own total. In the final «Completar visita» (Complete visit) confirmation you see them separately, with the liquor one marked «· licor» (· liquor).

- If you go back to the Order step and add more, new liquor is added to the liquor order and everything else to the other one. A third order is never created.

- «Compartir presupuesto» (Share quote) also comes out as two documents: it asks which one to share, «Compartir el de licor» (Share the liquor one) or «Compartir el otro» (Share the other one). The customer never gets a mixed document.

At companies without that rule, none of this happens.

Don’t get this wrong
Each order is a separate document at the office, with its own number. In [Activity › Orders](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html) you’ll see them separately, and they can move at different speeds: one may be confirmed while the other is still waiting for an analyst.

Don’t get this wrong
The price you see is a quote, not the invoice. The office recalculates prices and taxes when it receives the order, using the ones in effect the day it arrives. If the number changes, the app lets you know later in [Activity › Orders](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html).

Heads up
Two messages you’ll see that mean different things:

- «Total sin impuestos» (Total before tax) — the taxes for those products haven’t been downloaded yet. The order is sent anyway and the office calculates them. Tell the customer that isn’t the final total.

- «Sin precio» (No price), or a product at zero — that one can’t be sent. Remove it from the order or ask the office to load a price for it.

### Step 4 — Photos

Photos of the shelf, the display, anything you want to keep as proof of the visit. Tap «Tomar foto» (Take photo) and then «Agregar otra foto» (Add another photo). Up to 5 photos per visit. It opens the rear camera.

Don’t get this wrong
The photo is not required. The screen says so: «Sin fotos — paso opcional» (“No photos — optional step”). If your phone’s camera fails or the app closes when you open it, just keep going: the order, the stock count and the signature are saved anyway and the visit closes complete.

### Step 5 — Returns

Goods the customer is returning to you: expired, broken, shipped by mistake. At the top it says «Unidades a devolver» (Units to return) and at the bottom the «Total devoluciones» (Returns total) builds up.

If there’s nothing to return, leave everything at zero and move on. It isn’t a required step.

The reason goes inside the product card. Screenshot from 5.2.9: today the «De la devolución» (For the return) block sits above the list and the remarks are required (see below).

### How to put it together

- Find the product Search for it by name or code in the bar at the top, or scan it. It’s the same list as in the Order step.

- Set the quantity With the «+». As soon as it’s above zero, the card opens and shows what’s described below.

- Say why it’s coming back The suggested reasons — «Producto vencido» (Expired product), «Producto dañado / roto» (Damaged / broken product)… — fill themselves in when you tap them, and the row scrolls sideways: there are more than you can see. «Motivo (opcional)» (Reason, optional) is for writing it in your own words, and what you write takes precedence over the suggested one.

- Repeat for each product Each one gets its own reason. Two products coming back for different reasons are recorded as exactly that.

- And what applies to the whole return Above the list, under «De la devolución» (For the return): the remarks and «Foto de la devolución» (Return photo). The block is always there, even if you have a hundred products; until you enter units it’s grayed out and says «Carga unidades para agregar observaciones y fotos» (“Enter units to add remarks and photos”).

The remarks are required
When there are units to return, you have to write the remarks, and what they ask for is the affected invoice and order: the field reminds you with «Indica la factura y el pedido afectados» (“Enter the affected invoice and order”). It’s what the person approving the pickup reads, and what the warehouse checks against when the goods arrive.

Without them, «Guardar y continuar» (Save and continue) won’t let you through and tells you in red: «Escribe la factura y el pedido afectados para poder seguir» (“Enter the affected invoice and order to continue”). Photos are still optional: up to 5, and the button keeps count of how many you’ve taken.

The photo is your backup
If the goods are dented or expired, photograph them right there. That’s what backs up the return when the warehouse counts it and it doesn’t match what you said. The photo travels attached to the return, not to the order.

### Where it goes next

The return isn’t part of the order: it travels on its own and has a life of its own. This is the path it follows:

Where it is What it means

Por enviar (To send) It’s on your phone. It goes out by itself as soon as you get a signal.

En la oficina (At the office) It arrived and was logged. The warehouse hasn’t counted the goods yet.

Recibida (Received) The warehouse has checked it and accepted it.

You track it in Actividad › Devoluciones (Activity › Returns), with its reference number, the date and how many units it has. When the goods need to be picked up from the customer, that’s also where you see how the pickup is going: whether it was approved, whether someone has already collected the goods and whether the credit note has been issued. It’s explained in [Activity › Picking up the goods](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#retiro).

Don’t get this wrong
Sending it doesn’t mean it’s been received. Between «En la oficina» and «Recibida» the warehouse is counting the goods, and that can take days.

Don’t promise the customer an immediate credit note. What you can safely tell them is that the return was recorded, and under what number.

### Step 6 — Notes

There are two notes, and they go to two different places. That’s the most important thing about this step.

Field Who reads it

«Nota interna (solo para la oficina)» (Internal note, office only) Only your analyst. The customer never sees it.

«Nota del pedido (va en el documento)» (Order note, printed on the document) The customer, printed on the order slip.

Above the internal note there are ready-made phrases: «Cliente con mercancía» (Customer has stock), «Con deuda» (Has debt), «Pedido montado» (Order placed), «Volver próx. semana» (Come back next week)… Tap them and they’re added for you. It saves typing out in the sun. You can still write whatever you want on top.

Don’t get this wrong
The two notes never mix. Getting it wrong costs you either way: a private remark of yours about the customer printed on the paper they read, or a delivery condition the customer never hears about.

### Step 7 — Signature

Ask the customer to sign with their finger in the box. If the space is too small, tap «Firmar en pantalla completa» (Sign full screen) and the phone turns sideways. Didn’t come out right? «Limpiar firma» (Clear signature) and try again.

The signature is kept as backup for the visit in the company’s records.

Don’t get this wrong
The signature isn’t required either. The step’s title says «Firma (opcional)» (Signature, optional). If the customer isn’t there or doesn’t want to sign, continue: the visit and the order are still sent complete.

### Step 8 — Check-out

This is the «Resumen de visita» (Visit summary): everything you put together, in one place, so you can review it before sending. The order with its total, subtotal and VAT, the returns, both notes, the arrival time, how long the visit lasted, how many products you counted and how many photos you took.

Go over it with the customer. It’s your last chance to fix anything. You can go back with the arrow at the top.

When everything’s right, tap «Completar visita» (Complete visit). If the visit has no order, the button says «Finalizar visita sin pedido» (Finish visit without an order). A final question appears, «¿Completar la visita?» (Complete the visit?), with the details of what’s being sent: tap «Sí, completar» (Yes, complete).

The number of products in the order is shown with its units, so you don’t confuse lines with what the customer is taking: «2 productos · 3 unidades» (2 products · 3 units). If you used pack sizes, each one appears by name and they aren’t added together: «2 productos · 2 CAJ12 · 1 unidad» (2 products · 2 cases of 12 · 1 unit). You see it the same way in the final question, in the check-out «Detalle» (Details), on the confirmation screen and in the order PDF.

Heads up
If it warns you that some products «NO se envían» (are NOT being sent) because they were removed from the catalog, read it before you confirm: those won’t reach the office, and the customer is expecting them.

### If you leave in the middle of a visit

You don’t lose anything. The app saves what you’ve done — quantities, photos, notes, the signature — as you work. There’s no save button.

When you open that customer again, it asks «Visita en progreso» (Visit in progress) and tells you which step you were on. You have three options:

- «Continuar la visita» (Continue the visit) — you pick up where you left off.

- «Crear otro pedido» (Create another order) — you start a new one and the saved one stays intact.

- «Borrar y empezar de cero» (Delete and start over) — what you had is thrown away.

And you’ll find them all in [Activity › Orders › «Abiertos» (Open)](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/actividad.html#abiertos). Each one tells you when you started it and which step it’s on.

Heads up
If a visit has been open for hours and nobody touched the phone, when you complete it the app asks «Esta visita lleva mucho abierta» (“This visit has been open a long time”) and lets you choose which time to close it with: your last activity or now. That way you don’t end up with a four-hour visit that lasted twenty minutes.

### What happens when you complete it

With signal, the app sends the visit and shows you «¡Visita enviada!» (“Visit sent!”). The order is at the office, waiting for your analyst’s approval. That’s normal.

Don’t get this wrong
Without signal, the visit closes anyway. You’ll see «Tu visita quedó guardada — No hay internet ahora mismo. La mando apenas haya señal» (“Your visit was saved — There’s no internet right now. I’ll send it as soon as there’s signal”). You don’t have to do anything else: the app sends it by itself when you get coverage, even if you closed the app or turned off the phone. You can move on to the next stop with peace of mind.

Either way, you can keep following the order in Actividad › Pedidos (Activity › Orders) and the return in Actividad › Devoluciones (Activity › Returns). Until it has left the phone, it says «Por enviar» (To send).

If the customer paid you during the visit, tap «Cobrarle» (Collect from them), below «Ir al inicio» (Go to Home): the collection opens with that customer already filled in. See [Collecting from a customer](https://zentrix.company/en/sales/docs/cobrar.html#empezar).

### If an order bounces and the visit is already at the office

It can happen that the visit reaches the office and one of its orders bounces — almost always because there wasn’t enough stock — and the app sends you back to the Order step to fix it. In that case:

- What already went through can’t be changed from the visit. The steps that traveled with the check-out — check-in, stock count, photos, return, notes and signature — become read-only, with the notice «Esta visita ya está en la oficina: solo puedes corregir el pedido que no entró» (“This visit is already at the office: you can only fix the order that didn’t go through”). You can scroll through and review them, but not edit them.

- With two orders, if one already arrived, that one can’t be touched either: the app tells you it already arrived and that any change you make wouldn’t reach it. To modify it, do it from Activity › Orders once the visit is closed; to add products, put them in another order.

- The one that didn’t go through can be fixed, and it’s sent from check-out as usual.

Anything that can’t be touched appears dimmed, in gray: the «+» and «−», the quantity, the pack size, the Notes fields, the return reason, «Tomar foto» (Take photo), the Check-in buttons and the signature buttons. If a button is gray, it’s not that your phone didn’t respond: nothing can be changed there anymore.

Remember
«Enviado» (Sent) is not «aprobado» (approved). The visit reaching the office doesn’t mean the order is confirmed or shipped. That’s up to your analyst.
