## [Receiving a return — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/devoluciones.html)

Receive a return in Zentrix Work: support has already approved it, so you count what the customer brought, take the required photo and record the receipt.

### Receiving a return

The customer brings back something they bought. Your job is to count what arrived and take the photo. That’s all.

### Receiving is not approving

Support approved the return before it reached you. You don’t decide whether the money is refunded: you only count.

Get this one right
If the top says «Soporte todavía no la autorizó» (“Support hasn’t authorized it yet”): «No recibas el producto.» (“Don’t accept the product.”)

You open returns from the call or from the Devoluciones (Returns) shortcut on the main screen.

An authorized return: the reason, what the customer wrote and the count, which starts at the authorized quantity.

### 1. Count what you were given

Each line starts at the authorized quantity, not at zero. Usually everything arrives and you don’t touch anything.

- If less arrived, lower the line with Uno menos (One less). The app marks «Falta 1» (“1 missing”).

- You can’t go above the authorized quantity. «De menos sí (anótalo abajo). De más no: soporte aprobó estas cantidades y recibir no es aprobar.» (“Fewer, yes (note it below). More, no: support approved these quantities, and receiving is not approving.”)

If the customer brings more than was authorized, don’t receive it in the app: tell your manager.

### 2. The photo is required

Take at least one photo of what you were given. «Es lo único que respalda a la tienda si después no cuadra.» (“It’s the only thing that backs up the store if the numbers don’t match later.”)

If you take a photo of the ID card, «Tómala solo si el cliente está de acuerdo.» (“Take it only if the customer agrees.”) After that, only the store manager can see that photo: if you can’t see a teammate’s, that’s normal.

### 3. If the count is off, write what happened

If you lowered a quantity, the «Qué pasó» (What happened) field is required. One line is enough: «Trajo una sola, la otra dice que la perdió…» (“Brought only one, says they lost the other…”). With a full count, it’s optional.

### 4. Record the receipt

- Tap «Registrar la recepción» (Record the receipt). «¿Registrar la recepción?» (“Record the receipt?”) tells you how many units you’re about to record. «Queda a tu nombre y con la hora, y no se deshace desde el teléfono.» (“It’s saved under your name with the time, and it can’t be undone from the phone.”)

- Tap «Sí, registrar» (Yes, record). If you’re not sure, Todavía no (Not yet).

«Todavía no se puede registrar» (It can’t be recorded yet)
Something is missing: the photo, the note, or a quantity is too high. The app tells you which. Fix it and tap again.

It worked if…
You see «Recepción registrada.» (“Receipt recorded.”) with how much you received and how many photos. Tap Listo (Done).


---

## [Quick questions — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/dudas.html)

Quick answers to common Zentrix Work questions: calls that don’t ring, a forgotten PIN or password, the server field, breaks, battery use and new phones.

### Quick questions

The most common questions at the store, answered in two lines. If yours isn’t here, ask your manager.

### Orders don’t ring on my phone

Is your shift on? When it’s off, it never rings. If it is on, check for an amber warning at the top or a red dot on the bell, and make [a test call](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html#probar).

### I forgot my PIN

Tap ¿Olvidaste tu PIN? (Forgot your PIN?) and sign in with your email. You won’t lose your shift or any work in progress. [Step by step](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entrar.html#olvide-pin).

### I forgot my password

Ask your manager to reset it. If you know it and want to change it: Tu perfil › Cambiar mi contraseña (Your profile › Change my password).

### What do I enter under «Servidor» (Server)?

The full domain your manager gave you. Just the domain, with nothing after it. You type it once per phone.

### A task doesn’t show up

You haven’t been authorized for it. Tell your manager: it’s fixed in the system, not on your phone.

### My shift turned off by itself

Your phone went a long time without sending a signal, or the store closed. See [the two clocks](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/turno.html#solo). Start your shift again and carry on.

### I’m on and nothing comes in

There may be no work: «Nada pendiente. Cuando entre un pedido, te suena.» (“Nothing pending. When an order comes in, it’ll ring.”) If you see «Sin conexión: el trabajo nuevo no te llega» (“No connection: new work isn’t reaching you”), find a signal. If you’re on a break, tap Volver ya (Back now).

### I’m going to eat. Should I end my shift?

No: take a 5, 10 or 15-minute [break](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/turno.html#pausa). Work you’ve already started stays yours.

### Should I sign out at the end of the day?

No. Just end your shift. Signing out removes your account from the phone and asks for your email next time.

### I get a message and it won’t let me continue

Read it: the system writes it for you and says what’s missing. The app can’t skip it. If you think it’s a mistake, tell your manager.

### The top says «PRUEBAS» (TEST)

You’re on a test server, not in the real store. Tell your manager.

### Does it drain my battery?

As little as possible. The screen stays on only while a task is open, and when your shift is off it does nothing. The dark theme uses less.

### I lost my phone or got a new one

Tell your manager. On the new phone, install the app and sign in with the server, your email and your password.

None of this? Check [Support](https://zentrix.company/en/support/#work).


---

## [Signing in — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entrar.html)

Sign in to Zentrix Work: enter the server, your email and password once per phone, create your PIN, use your fingerprint, and what to do if you forget your PIN.

### Signing in: the first time and every day

You type your email and password only once on each phone. After that, you sign in with your PIN or your fingerprint.

### The first time

The sign-in screen. The server goes at the top, before your email.

- Type the server. It’s the full domain your manager gave you. Just the domain: nothing before it and nothing after it. The field starts empty on purpose.

- Type your email and password. The ones for your operator account. Your manager gives them to you. Tap the eye to see the password.

- Tap «Entrar» (Sign in). If your account uses two-step verification, type the 6-digit code sent to your email or your authenticator app.

Get this one right
The server decides where your password goes. Type it yourself, carefully, and only the one your manager gave you. If you see the PRUEBAS (TEST) badge at the top of the app, you’re not in the real store: tell your manager.

### If you get a message

Message What to do

«Correo o contraseña incorrectos.» (“Wrong email or password.”) Check there’s no space at the end. If it keeps happening, talk to your manager.

«Eso no parece un dominio. Escríbelo completo, como tutienda.com.» (“That doesn’t look like a domain. Type the whole thing, like yourstore.com.”) Type the entire domain, including its ending.

«Escribe solo el dominio, sin rutas ni nada detrás.» (“Type only the domain, with no paths or anything after it.”) Delete whatever comes after the domain.

«Sin conexión. Revisa tu internet e intenta de nuevo.» (“No connection. Check your internet and try again.”) It’s not your password: it’s the signal. Find Wi-Fi or mobile data.

The server stays saved even if the password fails. You don’t have to type it again.

### Create your PIN

- Choose a PIN of 4 to 8 digits. You use it to unlock the app on this phone.

- Enter it again. If it doesn’t match, the app says «No coincide. Vuelve a empezar.» (“It doesn’t match. Start over.”)

Your PIN is not your password
Your PIN lives only on your phone and never leaves it. Your password belongs to your account. They’re two different things.

### Every day

Open the app and it greets you by name. Type your PIN or use your fingerprint. The fingerprint prompt appears on its own when you open the app; if it doesn’t, tap Usar huella (Use fingerprint).

If you get it wrong: «PIN incorrecto. Intenta de nuevo.» (“Wrong PIN. Try again.”) After 10 failed attempts the keypad locks and you have to sign in with your email. Your fingerprint still works.

### If you forgot your PIN

- Tap «¿Olvidaste tu PIN?» (Forgot your PIN?). It shows up below the keypad as soon as you enter a wrong PIN.

- Tap «Entrar con mi correo» (Sign in with my email). The app tells you: «Vuelve a entrar con tu correo y elige un PIN nuevo. No pierdes tu turno ni tu trabajo a medias.» (“Sign in again with your email and choose a new PIN. You won’t lose your shift or any work in progress.”)

- Sign in with your email and password, and create a new PIN. The server is already saved.

«Entrar con otra cuenta» (Sign in with another account) is something else
That button, also on the PIN screen, clears the session from the phone and ends your shift. Use it only if someone else is really going to sign in. For a forgotten PIN, use ¿Olvidaste tu PIN?.

### If it asks you to update

Sometimes the app shows «Actualiza Zentrix Work» (“Update Zentrix Work”) and won’t let you continue. Tap Actualizar en Play (Update on Play), install the update and open the app again.

It worked if…
After the PIN you see the permissions (only the first time), and then «Hola» (“Hi”) with your name and «Elige tu tienda» (“Choose your store”).


---

## [Handing over in store — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entregar.html)

Hand over an order at the counter with Zentrix Work: check the pickup code, scan the packages, verify legal age for alcohol, take the proof photo and close it.

### Handing over in store

The customer is right in front of you. Ask for the code, scan the packages, take the proof photo if needed and hand it over. The button at the bottom walks you through it step by step.

### 1. Ask for the pickup code

Before you bring down a single package, ask the customer for their pickup code. You have it in big letters at the top of the order. If it doesn’t match, don’t hand it over and call your manager.

### If the customer shows up without a call

Tap Validar un código (Check a code) on the main screen. Point at the customer’s code, or type it if they read it to you, and tap Buscar (Search). The app tells you what it is and takes you there: Ir a la entrega (Go to the handover).

A counter handover: the pickup code in big letters and, at the bottom, the step that’s left.

### 2. Follow the button at the bottom

You only see the steps that order needs, in this order:

Leer los bultos (Scan the packages) → Verificar mayoría de edad (Verify legal age) → Tomar la foto de la prueba (Take the proof photo) → Entregar (Hand over)

### 3. Scan the packages

- Tap «Leer los bultos» (Scan the packages). «Apunta a la etiqueta del bulto.» (“Point at the package label.”) The count goes up: «2 de 3 bultos leídos» (“2 of 3 packages scanned”). If there’s only one, it says «Lee el bulto.» (“Scan the package.”) and «0 de 1 bulto leído» (“0 of 1 package scanned”).

- Scan them all, one by one. Even if they’re together. If a label won’t scan, tap A mano (By hand) and type the code.

If the order has no labels: «Este pedido no tiene bultos etiquetados: entrégalo con el chequeo manual de siempre.» (“This order has no labeled packages: hand it over with the usual manual check.”) Count them by hand.

If the rider already took it
On a delivery order that has already left, the screen says «El motorizado ya se lo llevó. No tienes que entregar nada más» (“The rider already took it. You don’t need to hand over anything else”) and who took it. The Entregar (Hand over) button doesn’t appear there: the rider closes the delivery at the customer’s door.

### 4. Orders with alcohol: check the age

If you see «Este pedido lleva bebidas alcohólicas» (“This order contains alcoholic beverages”), you have to verify the customer is of legal age before handing it over. It’s recorded under your name.

- Tap «Verificar la edad» (Verify age). Choose the document: Cédula (ID card), Licencia (Driver’s license) or Pasaporte (Passport).

- Place the document inside the frame and scan it. The app guides you: «Acerca la cédula al marco» (“Move the ID closer to the frame”), «Hay poca luz» (“The light is low”). «La foto no se guarda: solo se lee la fecha de nacimiento y se descarta.» (“The photo isn’t saved: only the date of birth is read, then it’s discarded.”)

- If it won’t scan, type the date. Tap Escribir la fecha a mano (Type the date by hand) and enter the day, month and year as shown on the document.

- Compare it with the document in your hand. The app tells you the age. Double-check it.

- Check «Vi el documento del cliente y es mayor de edad.» (I saw the customer’s document and they’re of legal age.) and tap «Confirmo que es mayor de edad» (I confirm they’re of legal age). Without the checkbox, the button stays off.

Get this one right

- If the app says they’re underage: «No entregues el pedido. Avisa al encargado.» (“Don’t hand over the order. Tell your manager.”)

- If the date is very close to 18, it asks you to type it yourself.

- Never check the box without seeing the document. Your confirmation is saved with your name and the time.

On a delivery order viewed in the store, it may say «La cédula la pide el conductor en la puerta.» (“The driver asks for the ID at the door.”) In that case, it’s not your job.

### 5. The proof photo

Tap Paquete (Package) or Cédula (ID card) and take the photo. Check «¿Se ve bien?» (“Does it look good?”) and tap Usar esta foto (Use this photo).

- If the order requires it, it says obligatoria (required): «Este pedido no se puede entregar sin al menos una foto.» (“This order can’t be handed over without at least one photo.”)

- If not, it’s optional: «Puedes dejar constancia con una foto del paquete o de la cédula de quien recibe.» (“You can keep a record with a photo of the package or of the recipient’s ID.”)

The ID card is sensitive data
The photo of the ID stays with the order, under your name. Take it only if the customer agrees. If they don’t want to, the package photo works.

### 6. Hand it over

- Give them the packages and tap «Entregar» (Hand over). «¿Entregar el pedido?» (“Hand over the order?”) reminds you how many packages and to whom. «El pedido queda cerrado y no se puede deshacer desde el teléfono.» (“The order is closed and can’t be undone from the phone.”)

- Tap «Sí, entregar» (Yes, hand over). If you’re not sure, Todavía no (Not yet).

It worked if…
You see «Entregado.» (“Handed over.”) and how long it took you. Tap Listo (Done). The order won’t come back to your list.

Collecting payment at the door and «No pude entregar» (I couldn’t deliver) belong to [home delivery](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/reparto.html), not the counter.


---

## [Zentrix Work documentation — For store teams](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/)

The Zentrix Work documentation for store teams, step by step: signing in, your shift, picking orders with the scanner, delivery runs, returns and settings.

### Operator documentation

What’s new in version 1.1.7. The app is now called Zentrix Work and has a new look: light theme by default, the Inter typeface and a new icon.

- There’s only one promised time, the system’s: the list, the details and «Es tuya» (It’s yours) all say the same thing, in the format «8:19 p. m.». See [Picking an order](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/preparar.html#orden).

- The 15-minute break says 15, not 16, and below «Desliza para apagar» (Swipe to end) it now says «Al apagarte, tu teléfono deja de sonar.» (“When you go off, your phone stops ringing.”) See [Your shift](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/turno.html).

- If you start your shift on another phone, the first one shuts off right away, on any screen.

- If the rider already took the order, «Entregar» (Hand over) no longer appears. See [Handing over in store](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entregar.html#edad).

- The «No puedo» (I can’t) reasons depend on the type of call. See [Calls](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/llamada.html#no-puedo).

- «Cómo llegar» (Directions) no longer closes the app. See [Home delivery](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/reparto.html#navegar).

- Plurals spelled correctly: «1 bulto» (“1 package”), «1 Unidad» (“1 Unit”).

Some screenshots in this documentation still show the previous design, but the steps are the same.

Zentrix Work is the app for your company’s store team. Here’s how to use it, screen by screen, in short sentences you can read on your feet.

### What is Zentrix Work

It’s the app you use to handle your store’s work from your phone. It’s not the shopping app: that’s your company’s customer app. You can have both installed at the same time.

With it:

- You start your shift at a store and choose what you’ll handle.

- A call rings when there’s work for you.

- You pick orders, hand them over in store or deliver them to the door, and receive returns.

### It’s your phone

The app runs on your personal phone. That’s why it looks after your battery, your data and your privacy:

- Off means silent. With no shift on, you don’t get a single alert.

- Location only during your shift. When you start, when you end and while you work. Never outside of it.

- The screen stays on only while a task is open, not for your whole shift.

- Your PIN never leaves your phone. It’s a lock that lives only there.

### Who decides what you see

Your store manager gives you your account and authorizes your stores and tasks. The system is in charge: if something won’t let you through, the app tells you why with the server’s message, word for word. It’s not a problem with your phone.

Authorized is not switched on
For a task to ring for you, two things are needed: your manager has to authorize it, and you have to switch it on in today’s shift.

### The documentation

### Start here

- [Signing in: the first time and every day Server, email and password once. After that, PIN or fingerprint.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entrar.html)

- [Permissions and sound Notifications, location, camera, and making sure your phone isn’t on silent.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/permisos.html)

### Your shift

- [Your shift Choose a store and tasks, swipe to start, breaks and ending your shift.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/turno.html)

- [Calls 60 seconds to take it or say «No puedo» (I can’t).](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/llamada.html)

### The work

- [Picking an order Scan, mark what’s out of stock, packages and rack.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/preparar.html)

- [Handing over in store Pickup code, scanning packages, proof and age.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entregar.html)

- [Home delivery Load stops, your trip, navigate and hand over at the door.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/reparto.html)

- [Receiving a return Count what arrived and take the photo.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/devoluciones.html)

### Look it up

- [Your day and your performance What you’ve already closed today.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/tu-dia.html)

- [Settings Test a call, vibration, sound, flash and theme.](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html)

Can’t find what you need? Ask your manager or check [Support](https://zentrix.company/en/support/#work).

## [Calls — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/llamada.html)

How a Zentrix Work call works: it rings when there’s work for you, and you have 60 seconds to swipe and take it or tap «No puedo» (I can’t) to pass it on.

### Calls

With your shift on, when there’s work for you, your phone rings, vibrates and opens a screen by itself. You have 60 seconds to decide.

### What it looks like

A call to pick an order. At the top, what it is; in the middle, the order; at the bottom, the timer and your two options.

At the top, what you’re being asked to do. Each task has its own verb:

The top says To take it, you swipe

PREPARAR · Pedido nuevo (PICK · New order) Yo lo hago (I’ll do it)

ENTREGAR · Cliente esperando (HAND OVER · Customer waiting) Yo lo entrego (I’ll hand it over)

DEVOLUCIÓN · Devolución en la puerta (RETURN · Return at the door) Yo la atiendo (I’ll handle it)

PARADA NUEVA · Un pedido para llevarle al cliente (NEW STOP · An order to take to the customer) Yo la llevo (I’ll take it)

In the middle, the order: its reference and the customer, and for a handover also the pickup code, the packages and the rack. At the bottom, the timer: «45 s y pasa al siguiente» (“45 s until it moves on”). In the last 15 seconds it turns red.

The call comes through even if your phone is locked, and the flash blinks if you’ve turned it on in [Settings](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html).

### If you take it

- Drag the control («Yo lo entrego», «Yo lo hago»…) all the way across. You swipe it so that a bump in your pocket can’t accept a job you’re not going to do.

- Now it’s yours. The screen says «Es tuya. ¡Dale!» (“It’s yours. Go!”) with the order, how long until the promised time, and what comes next. That time is the same one you see in the list and in the order details.

- Tap the button for the job. Preparar el pedido (Pick the order), Abrir la entrega (Open the handover) or Abrir la parada (Open the stop). It takes you to the screen where you do the work.

After accepting a test call. In a real one, the button that opens the job sits above «Terminé» (I’m done).

The screen stays on
«Tu pantalla no se apaga mientras trabajas. Si guardas el teléfono, la tarea sigue visible en la pantalla de bloqueo.» (“Your screen stays on while you work. If you put your phone away, the task stays visible on the lock screen.”) Only while you have a task: once you finish it, everything goes back to normal. While a task is open, no other call will ring.

### If you can’t

- Tap «No puedo» (I can’t). Just one tap. The ringing stops: «Listo, se la pasamos a otro compañero.» (“Done, we’ll pass it to a teammate.”)

- If you want, say why. You may see «¿Por qué no puedes? (opcional)» (“Why can’t you? (optional)”) with reasons to tap. The system sends them based on the type of call: on a picking call you won’t see the delivery ones, like «El cliente no contesta» (The customer isn’t answering) or «Problema con la moto» (Problem with the motorcycle). It’s not required.

- Made a mistake? While there’s time left, tap Me equivoqué, sí puedo (My mistake, I can).

Don’t be afraid to say «No puedo»
Saying «No puedo» gets the work to someone who can do it faster. It’s better than letting the call time out.

### If you don’t answer

After 60 seconds the call moves on: «Pasó al siguiente operador.» (“It went to the next operator.”) The screen closes by itself. The order isn’t lost: someone else handles it.

If the main screen says «Hay … llamadas viejas en esta tienda que ya no suenan» (“There are … old calls at this store that no longer ring”), there’s work waiting. Check the list.

### The test call

In [Settings › Test a call](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html#probar), a call rings exactly like a real one, with the banner «PRUEBA — no es trabajo de verdad» (TEST — not real work). It doesn’t count and nobody else gets it. Do one on your first day.

It worked if…
You took the call and you’re on the job, or you said «No puedo» and the phone went quiet with your shift still on.


---

## [Permissions and sound — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/permisos.html)

The permissions Zentrix Work asks for and why: work alerts, approximate location and camera, plus how to make sure your phone actually rings when work comes in.

### Permissions and sound

The app asks for very little and tells you why. Without notifications, work won’t ring on your phone; without the camera, you type codes by hand.

### The three permissions

The first time, the app shows you «Para trabajar, la app te pide estos permisos» (“To work, the app needs these permissions”):

Permission What it’s for Required?

Avisos de trabajo (Work alerts) Without it, your phone won’t ring when an order is assigned to you, and after 60 seconds it goes to a teammate. Yes

Ubicación aproximada (Approximate location) To know you’re at the store during your shift. Only your general area. Yes

Cámara (Camera) It’s the scanner and the ID card reader. Optional

Tap the button for each one: Permitir los avisos (Allow alerts), Permitir la ubicación (Allow location), Permitir la cámara (Allow camera). When it’s done, it says «Listo, ya lo tienes.» (“Done, you’re all set.”)

If you don’t want to use the camera, tap Seguir sin la cámara (Continue without the camera). You’ll type codes and dates by hand.

### Your location

What the app says
«La ubicación se usa solo mientras tu turno está encendido, siempre aproximada, y lo guardado se borra a los 30 días. Con la app cerrada o fuera de turno no se mira dónde estás.» (“Location is used only while your shift is on, always approximate, and anything saved is deleted after 30 days. With the app closed or when you’re off shift, nobody looks at where you are.”)

For [home delivery](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/reparto.html), the map needs your precise location, and only while you have a stop open.

### Calls over the lock screen

You may see «La llamada no va a tapar la pantalla» (“Calls won’t cover the screen”). Without this permission the call still rings, but you have to unlock your phone to see it. Tap Dar el permiso (Grant permission).

### Make sure your phone rings

If something keeps your phone from ringing, the warning shows up at the top, in amber.

Before and during your shift, the app checks that your phone can ring. If something is wrong, a warning appears at the top with a button to fix it:

Warning Button

«Tu teléfono está en silencio» (“Your phone is on silent”) Abrir el sonido del teléfono (Open phone sound settings)

«Tu teléfono solo vibra» (“Your phone only vibrates”) Abrir el sonido del teléfono (Open phone sound settings)

«Tienes No Molestar prendido» (“Do Not Disturb is on”) Abrir No Molestar (Open Do Not Disturb)

«Tu teléfono no te va a avisar» (“Your phone won’t alert you”) Activar las notificaciones (Turn on notifications)

«Las llamadas están silenciadas» (“Calls are muted”) Activar el aviso de llamadas (Turn on call alerts)

The bell at the top warns you too: with a red dot it tells you «Tu teléfono no va a sonar» (“Your phone won’t ring”).

Heads up
If you turn off the app’s notifications, the system may not let you start your shift. The message appears on screen, word for word.

It worked if…
There’s no amber warning at the top. To be sure, make [a test call](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html#probar).

### If you said “no” to a permission

Your phone won’t ask again. Tap Abrir los ajustes de la app (Open app settings), grant it and come back: the app picks up on its own. If settings don’t open, go to Settings › Apps › Zentrix Work › Permissions.


---

## [Picking an order — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/preparar.html)

Pick an order in Zentrix Work step by step: scan products, mark what’s out of stock, ask the customer, count packages, place them on the rack and validate.

### Picking an order

Picking is one button at a time. At the bottom, in big letters, there’s always the next step. Do what the button says and the button changes by itself.

### The order of steps, always the same

Comenzar preparación (Start picking) → Escanear productos (Scan products) → Preguntar al cliente (Ask the customer) → ¿En cuántos bultos va? (How many packages?) → Dónde quedó el bulto (Where the package went) → Validar la preparación (Validate the picking)

«Preguntar al cliente» only appears if something was missing.

The order’s time
Every order has a badge with its time: «faltan 12 min» (“12 min left”) or «18 min tarde» (“18 min late”). Green means you’re on time, amber means it’s about to be late, red means it’s late. Handle the red ones first.

Next to it is the time promised to the customer: «para las 8:19 p. m.» (“by 8:19 p.m.”). There’s only one, the one the system gives, and it’s the same in the list, in the order details and on «Es tuya» (It’s yours).

An order halfway through picking: what’s left, the promised time and each product with its count.

### 1. Start

Open the order from the call or from the list. Tap Comenzar preparación (Start picking). The order is now in your name and the customer gets a notice that you’re picking it.

### 2. Scan the products

- Tap «Escanear productos» (Scan products). The camera opens. If the light is low, use the flashlight.

- Scan each barcode. The app tells you how many you have: «X de Y» (“X of Y”). When it’s complete: «ya tienes lo pedido» (“you have everything ordered”).

- If it won’t scan, type it in. Tap A mano (By hand) on the scanner, or the keyboard next to the button at the bottom.

With no signal, your scans are saved on the phone and upload by themselves when you’re back online. If anything is still saved at the end, the button says Subir … escaneos guardados (Upload … saved scans).

Expired or expiring lot
If an amber card shows up with a lot, do what it says: «Agarra otra caja» (“Grab another box”), «Revisa la fecha antes de recogerlo» (“Check the date before you pick it”) or «Avisa al encargado» (“Tell your manager”). With Cambiar lote (Change lot) you choose another one.

### 3. When something isn’t there: «No hay»

- Open the product’s line and tap «No hay» (Out of stock). The app asks «¿No hay?» (“Out of stock?”). Tap Sí, no hay (Yes, it’s out).

- Check the replacement. The system suggests an equivalent: «Anotado. Equivalente sugerido: …» (“Noted. Suggested equivalent: …”). The line stays marked «No hay», in plain sight.

One question per order
Mark every missing item before you ask. The Preguntar al cliente (N faltantes) (Ask the customer (N missing)) button asks once about all of them.

### 4. Ask the customer

Tap Preguntar al cliente (Ask the customer). The message goes out by itself; you don’t type anything. «El cliente ya tiene la consulta de los faltantes. Su respuesta destranca la validación.» (“The customer has the question about the missing items. Their answer unlocks validation.”) Meanwhile, keep going with the rest.

### 5. How many packages?

Count the bags or boxes you packed and enter the number. You don’t need to say which product goes in which. Confirm with Van en N bultos (It’s N packages).

If you already printed labels
Changing the number makes the old labels invalid: peel them off and reprint the full set.

### 6. Where the package went

Put each package on the rack and tell the app which position: «Bulto 1 de 3 — ¿en qué posición del rack lo pusiste?» (“Package 1 of 3 — which rack position did you put it in?”). It asks one package at a time.

No position, no validation
Every package needs its position before you validate. If they all show «ocupada» (“taken”), don’t make one up: tell your manager.

### 7. Validate the picking

- Tap «Validar la preparación» (Validate the picking). The app tells you how many packages and how many missing items there are. «Sale del inventario y no se puede deshacer desde el teléfono.» (“It comes out of inventory and can’t be undone from the phone.”)

- Tap «Sí, validar» (Yes, validate). If something doesn’t add up, Todavía no (Not yet).

- Stick on the labels. «Recoge la etiqueta de la impresora y pégala al bulto.» (“Take the label from the printer and stick it on the package.”) Tap Listo (Done).

If it won’t let you validate, the app tells you why, in the system’s words. If it’s waiting on the customer’s answer, leave the order and move on to another one: it unlocks by itself when they reply.

### If you have to drop the order

In the Más (More) menu, tap Dejar este pedido (Drop this order). Choose the reason under «¿Por qué lo dejas?» (“Why are you dropping it?”) and tap Dejar el pedido (Drop the order). It goes back to the store’s queue for another teammate.

It worked if…
You see «Preparación validada.» (“Picking validated.”), every package has its label and its spot on the rack, and the order has left your list.


---

## [Home delivery — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/reparto.html)

Deliver orders with Zentrix Work: load stops at the store, sort your trip, navigate to the customer, collect cash on delivery and report when you can’t deliver.

### Home delivery

Stops are loaded at the store, with the engine off. Out on the street, you only deliver. Learn that rule and you’ll never waste a trip.

### Your two doors

If you handle Reparto (Delivery), with your shift on you see two doors on the main screen:

- Paradas (Stops) — «Los pedidos que llevas a la calle» (“The orders you take out on the street”). This is the store: what’s waiting to be loaded.

- Mi viaje (My trip) — «Lo que llevas, en tu orden» (“What you’re carrying, in your order”). This is your vehicle: only your stuff.

A new stop can also come to you as a [call](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/llamada.html). There, the control says Yo la llevo (I’ll take it).

A diagram, not a screenshot: you load at the store, you deliver on the street.

### Load your trip

- Open «Mi viaje» (My trip). With an empty trip it says: «Todavía no llevas nada. Carga las paradas aquí, en la tienda: en la calle no se hace.» (“You’re not carrying anything yet. Load your stops here, at the store: it’s not done on the street.”)

- Under «Para cargar» (To load), tap the stop you’re taking. One tap and it goes onto your trip, at the end of the list.

- Check the bar at the top. «Llevas 2 de 4» (“2 of 4 loaded”) and «caben 2 más» (“room for 2 more”). The store sets the limit, not you.

When you’re full: «Tu viaje está lleno. Sal a repartir: cuando cierres una parada, te cabe otra.» (“Your trip is full. Head out and deliver: when you close a stop, you’ll have room for another.”) You free up room by closing stops.

If it won’t let you load it
It may say «Esa parada ya tiene dueño» (“That stop already has an owner”). «Desde aquí no se la puedes quitar: el relevo lo hace el encargado. Carga otra parada y sigue.» (“You can’t take it from them here: your manager handles reassignments. Load another stop and keep going.”) Tap Elegir otra parada (Choose another stop).

### Put them in your order

You set the order. You change it by dragging the three lines (≡) on the right of each stop.

Get this one right
Pressing and holding the card doesn’t move it. And tapping the card opens it. The handle is the three lines and nothing else.

Stop number 1 is the active one. There’s nothing to save: the order sticks when you let go.

### Remove a stop from your trip

Tap the stop’s Sacarla del viaje (Remove from trip) button. The app asks «¿Por qué la sacas?» (“Why are you removing it?”) and shows you the reasons the store provides, or Otro motivo (Other reason) to type your own. The stop goes back to the store’s queue. If you change your mind, Sigo con ella (I’ll keep it).

### A new stop while you’re driving

If you’re offered a stop while the vehicle is moving, the app doesn’t cover your screen. The phone vibrates and says out loud «Tienes una parada nueva. Se abre al detenerte.» (“You have a new stop. It opens when you stop.”)

When you stop, it opens by itself. You can also tap the notice «Hay una parada nueva para ti» (“There’s a new stop for you”) in My trip or on the map.

### Navigate to the customer

The stop you’re taking: the address with «Cómo llegar» (Directions) and, at the bottom, the step that’s left.

- On the stop, tap «Cómo llegar» (Directions). It’s on the address card, «A dónde va» (“Where it’s going”), with its landmark.

- Tap «Navegar» (Navigate). Turn-by-turn guidance runs inside the app. The first time, it asks for precise location and for you to accept Google’s terms.

- Follow the guidance. If you leave it, you get back with Seguir navegando (Keep navigating).

You also always have Abrir en Google Maps (Open in Google Maps).

If «Cómo llegar» used to close the app
That happened in earlier versions. Since 1.1.7, the map opens and the app stays open. If it still happens to you, check at the store that you have the latest version.

- The route is for cars, not motorcycles: Google doesn’t offer two-wheeler routes in Venezuela yet.

- Without data, the map only keeps about 15 to 20 minutes ahead. After that, the guidance goes quiet.

- Address with no pin on the map: go by the street and the landmark. That’s normal, not an error.

### How much it talks

On the map you choose «Mudo» (Muted), «Solo avisos» (Alerts only) or «Guía completa» (Full guidance). With «Avisos de Zentrix Work» (Zentrix Work alerts) on, it tells you which order you’ve arrived at, how much to collect and whether it requires an ID. The guidance always speaks Spanish.

Your location during deliveries
It’s only shared while you have a stop open, with the «Ruta en curso» (Route in progress) notice on. When you close the last one, it turns off. Anything saved is deleted after 30 days.

### At the customer’s door

The stop screen is the same as for [handing over in store](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/entregar.html): pickup code, packages, age if there’s alcohol, payment and proof. The button at the bottom always shows the step that’s left:

Leer los bultos (Scan the packages) → Verificar mayoría de edad (Verify legal age) → Declarar el cobro (Record the payment) → Tomar la foto de la prueba (Take the proof photo) → Entregar (Hand over)

Only the steps that order needs appear. Always ask the customer for their pickup code before you let go of anything.

### Collect cash on delivery

If the order is paid at the door, you see «Cobra … en la puerta» (“Collect … at the door”) with the amount and payment method: Efectivo (Cash) or Datáfono (Card terminal). The system sets the amount and method; you don’t calculate anything.

- Collect the exact amount. If there’s an equivalent in bolívars, the app shows it to you.

- Tap «Declarar el cobro» (Record the payment). With a card terminal, it may ask for the Foto del voucher (Receipt photo) and the Referencia de la operación (Transaction reference), the number the terminal gives you.

- Tap «Ya cobré» (I’ve collected it). It turns on once everything it needs is there. It shows «Cobro declarado. Queda a tu nombre hasta que lo entregues.» (“Payment recorded. It stays under your name until you turn it in.”)

Get this one right

- Never type the card number. Only the reference.

- «Si el cliente no tiene el monto exacto, no cobres de menos: usa «No pude entregar».» (“If the customer doesn’t have the exact amount, don’t collect less: use ‘I couldn’t deliver’.”)

- The money you collect is your responsibility until you turn it in at the store. The app reminds you how much you’re carrying.

### If you can’t deliver

Nobody answers, the address doesn’t exist, the customer doesn’t want it, the payment couldn’t be collected. It’s not your fault, and waiting on the sidewalk won’t fix it: report it.

- Tap «No pude entregar» (I couldn’t deliver). It’s on the same stop screen.

- Choose the reason under «¿Qué pasó?» (What happened?). The three most common ones appear. The rest are under Otro motivo (Other reason). The store provides the list.

- Fill in what it asks for. Depending on the reason: a photo, or «Qué pasó» (“What happened”) in a few words. If it asks for location, turn it on.

- Tap «Reportarlo» (Report it). It turns on once everything is filled in. If you can deliver after all, Sí puedo entregar (I can deliver).

Unsafe area
«Para esto no hace falta foto. No te expongas sacando el teléfono: repórtalo y sigue.» (“No photo needed for this. Don’t put yourself at risk by taking out your phone: report it and move on.”) Your safety comes first.

After you report it, the screen tells you what to do, in the store’s own words. Reporting doesn’t cancel the order or touch the money: a person decides. In the meantime, don’t hand over or return anything on your own. Tap Listo (Done) and move on to your next stop.

It worked if…
After Sí, entregar (Yes, hand over) you see «Entregado.» (“Handed over.”) and the stop leaves your trip. You’ll have room for another one next time you’re at the store.


---

## [Your day and your performance — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/tu-dia.html)

What «Mi trabajo de hoy» (My work today) shows in Zentrix Work: what you closed today or this week, how much was on time, your pace and your level.

### Your day and your performance

In «Mi trabajo de hoy» (My work today) you see what you’ve already closed. Only what YOU closed counts.

### How to open it

On the main screen, with your shift on, tap Mi trabajo de hoy (My work today) — «Lo que ya cerraste» (“What you’ve already closed”). At the top, choose Hoy (Today) or Esta semana (This week). Swipe down to refresh.

### The scoreboard

The big number is how many jobs you closed. Below it, broken down: Preparados (Picked), Entregados (Handed over), Devueltos (Returned) and A tiempo (On time).

Further down, the list by day (Hoy, Ayer (Yesterday), the date), with packages, items and how long each one took you.

If there’s nothing yet: «Todavía no has cerrado nada hoy.» (“You haven’t closed anything yet today.”) «Lo que termines aparece aquí.» (“What you finish shows up here.”)

### How you’re doing

For each task you see how many you closed, your typical time and what percentage was on time.

Your pace is not a target
«La mitad de tus trabajos tardó menos que eso. Es tu ritmo normal, no una meta.» (“Half of your jobs took less than that. It’s your normal pace, not a target.”)

You also see your shifts and hours worked, and how many of the times your area was checked showed you at the store.

### Your level

Once the system has your track record, the TU NIVEL (YOUR LEVEL) card appears: Bronce (Bronze), Plata (Silver), Oro (Gold) or Platino (Platinum), with your score and how long you’ve had it.

Below, it tells you what you need for the next one: «Te faltan N trabajos.» (“You need N more jobs.”) or «Te falta subir tu puntuación N puntos.» (“You need to raise your score by N points.”) Those numbers are calculated by the system, not your phone.

If there’s no track record yet, the card doesn’t appear. That’s not an error.


---

## [Your shift — Zentrix Work documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/turno.html)

Start your shift in Zentrix Work: choose your store and tasks, swipe to go on, take 5 to 15-minute breaks, end your shift, and see when it turns off by itself.

### Your shift

When it’s on, your store’s work comes to you. When it’s off, your phone doesn’t ring. Sign in, choose and swipe: it takes less than a minute.

### Start your shift

Check-in: your store, your tasks and the control to start your shift.

- Tap your store under «Elige tu tienda» (Choose your store). If you only have one, it’s already selected.

- Under «¿Qué vas a atender hoy?» (What will you handle today?), leave on what you’re going to do. Pedidos (Orders), Entregas (Handovers), Devoluciones (Returns) or Reparto (Delivery). You only see the ones you’re authorized for. Whatever you switch off won’t ring for you.

- Drag «Desliza para encender» (Swipe to start) all the way across. You swipe it, you don’t tap it: that way it never turns on by accident. You’ll hear a rising tone.

If a task doesn’t show up
It isn’t switched off: you haven’t been authorized for it. Your manager fixes that, not your phone. If there are none at all, the app says «No tienes tareas autorizadas. Habla con el encargado.» (“You have no authorized tasks. Talk to your manager.”)

If the system won’t let you start your shift, a message at the bottom tells you why. Read it: it’s written for you.

### While your shift is on

Your shift, on. From top to bottom: status, break, task in progress, pending work and shortcuts.

- «ESTÁS ACTIVO» (YOU’RE ON): your store, since what time («desde las 7:34 p. m.», “since 7:34 p.m.”) and what you’re handling. Below it, the store hours: «cierra a las … · tu turno se apaga al cierre» (“closes at … · your shift ends at closing”).

- «AHORA MISMO» (RIGHT NOW): how many jobs are waiting and what’s next, with its time badge («faltan 32 min», “32 min left”). If something is running late, you see it in red as «atrasados» (“late”). Tap Ver el trabajo (See the work) to open the list.

- The shortcuts: Devoluciones (Returns), Validar un código (Check a code), Mi trabajo de hoy (My work today), and if you do deliveries, Paradas (Stops) and Mi viaje (My trip).

If you have a job in progress, «SIGUE DONDE LO DEJASTE» (PICK UP WHERE YOU LEFT OFF) appears at the top. Tap it to go back to it. If you took a call and haven’t finished it, you see the «Tarea en curso» (Task in progress) card, with how long ago you took it: tap it to go back to it.

To change stores or tasks: end your shift and start it again.

### Take a break

- Under «¿Necesitas un rato?» (Need a minute?), tap 5, 10 or 15 min. «Dejas de recibir trabajo nuevo y vuelves solo. No cierras tu turno ni sueltas lo que tengas empezado.» (“You stop getting new work and come back automatically. You don’t end your shift or drop anything you’ve started.”)

- Come back automatically, or tap «Volver ya» (Back now). On a break, the app says EN PAUSA (ON BREAK) and how much time you have left, rounded to the minute: if you asked for 15, it says 15, not 16. At the end it says «1 minuto» (“1 minute”) and then «menos de un minuto» (“less than a minute”).

To eat or use the restroom: take a break, don’t end your shift.

### End your shift when you’re done

Drag Desliza para apagar (Swipe to end), at the very bottom. Below the control, it reminds you: «Al apagarte, tu teléfono deja de sonar.» (“When you go off, your phone stops ringing.”) You hear a falling tone and you’re back at check-in, which says «Apagado, tu teléfono jamás suena.» (“When you’re off, your phone never rings.”)

Before ending your shift, finish whatever you’ve started.

Ending your shift is not signing out
To finish the day, end your shift. Cerrar sesión (Sign out), in your profile, removes your account from the phone: next time it asks for your email and password.

### When it turns off by itself

Every minute, your phone tells the system you’re still there. If it stops doing that, the system doesn’t wait forever. There are two clocks:

A diagram, not a screenshot: minutes without any signal from your phone.

- After 20 minutes you stop getting new work, but your shift stays open. It comes back on its own as soon as the app reconnects.

- After 90 minutes —or if 90 go by without anyone touching the app— your shift closes. You’ll need to check in again.

- When the store closes, your shift ends too.

- If you start your shift on another phone, the first one shuts off right away, on whatever screen it’s on: it plays the end-of-shift tone and goes back to check-in with the system’s notice. Your shift lives on one phone at a time.

When the system ends your shift, the screen goes back to check-in and plays the end-of-shift tone. The notice may stay in the bell.

Put simply
Twenty minutes means “we’re taking you out of the rotation for a while.” Ninety means “your shift is over.” If you’re going to be away from your phone, take a break or end your shift yourself.

### The header

- The bell («Avisos», “Alerts”): messages from customers, canceled or overdue orders, notices from your manager. With a red dot, your phone won’t ring.

- The gear: [Settings](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/ajustes.html).

- Your initials or your photo: «Tu perfil» (“Your profile”). There you see your store and what you can handle, change your password and sign out.


---

## [Zentrix Work — The app for store and delivery teams](https://zentrix.company/en/work/)

Zentrix Work, the Android app for store teams: work lands on the phone to pick orders, deliver, run delivery routes and take returns during the shift.

For store teams · Android

### Your shift, organized from your phone.

Clock in when you get to the store and the work comes to you: orders to pick, deliveries and returns. When you're done, clock out and your phone is yours again.

[Read the documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/)

An order rings. Swipe to take it.

How it works

### A shift with Zentrix Work.

No more watching for messages or asking what's next. The app lets you know, you decide whether to take it, and when you're done, everything is on record.

If it's your first day, the [documentation](https://zentrix.company/en/work/docs/) walks you through every screen with screenshots.

- Clock in at your store Check in and choose what you'll handle today: orders, deliveries or returns.

- An order rings Even with your screen off. You see what it is, its code and how many packages it has.

- Swipe to take it You have 60 seconds. If you can't, tap “I can't” and it goes to a teammate.

- Pick it or deliver it Scan item by item with your camera, package by package.

- Take a break if you need one 5, 10 or 15 minutes without closing your shift or dropping what you started.

- Clock out when you leave And if you forget, the shift closes on its own. Your phone stops ringing.

What it helps you do

### Fewer interruptions, fewer mistakes, more control.

Every feature is built for the real pace of a store: lots of movement, little time and a customer waiting.

- 01

### Pick orders
Pick item by item using your camera as a scanner, and the app tells you if anything is missing before you close.

- 02

### Deliver
At the counter or to the door, package by package, with proof of delivery on the spot.

- 03

### Receive returns
You only take back what support has already approved, so there's no arguing at the counter.

- 04

### Alerts you actually hear
If your phone is on silent, the app tells you and takes you straight to the fix.

- 05

### A shift with a start and an end
You work while you're clocked in. Off shift, nothing interrupts you.

- 06

### Fast, secure sign-in
Sign in once with your email, then with your PIN or fingerprint. Your PIN never leaves your phone.

Use cases

### One shift, three kinds of work.

When you clock in, you choose what you'll handle today. Here's how each one comes in.

- 01

### An order to pick
It rings even with your screen off. Take it with a swipe, pick it by scanning item by item, and the app warns you if anything is missing.

- 02

### A delivery
At the counter or to the door, package by package, with proof of delivery on the spot.

- 03

### A return
You only take back what support has already approved, so there's no arguing at the counter.

Screen by screen

### A shift, from the call to the handover.

Light for working in the sun, dark if you prefer.

Clock in and choose what you handle.

An order rings: swipe to take it.

The queue, most urgent first.

Prepare item by item.

Hand over with the pickup code.

Build your delivery trip.

Receive returns with photos.

Light or dark, your choice.

Real screenshots of the app (in Spanish), with a test store and test customers.

Your phone

### It's your phone, and we treat it that way.

The app runs on your personal phone, so it uses as little as possible and only works while you do.

- Clocked out, it stays quiet. With no active shift, you won't get a single notification.

- Location only during your shift. Never off shift or in the background, and it's deleted after 30 days.

- Easy on your battery. The screen stays on only while a task is open.

- No ads and no advertising ID.

[What data the app uses and why](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/)

### Who it's for

For store staff at companies that use Zentrix Work. There's no sign-up: your manager creates your account with the stores and tasks assigned to you. Anyone can install the app, but without an account it doesn't do anything.

### How to get started

- Ask your manager for access.

- Install Zentrix Work from Google Play.

- Enter the server, your email and your password. Only the first time.

- Create your PIN or use your fingerprint, and you're set.

### Download Zentrix Work

For Android. Questions? Write to us at [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Support%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Work).

## [Privacy policy — Zentrix Work](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/)

What the Zentrix Work app collects, why, who sees it and for how long, how it is protected, and how to ask for access to your data or for its deletion.

Legal

### Zentrix Work privacy policy

Last updated: October 13, 2026.

### 1. What Zentrix Work is and who it is for

Zentrix Work is the internal work tool for the store staff of the company that uses it (“the company” from here on). It is developed by GUUAO LLC and distributed through Google Play, for Android. Operators use it to pick orders, make deliveries and take in returns.

It is not a consumer app and it does not let anyone sign up. Accounts are created by a store manager for staff hired by the company. Without one, the app does nothing. If the company has an app for its customers, that is a different app with its own privacy policy.

This policy covers two groups of people:

- The operator: the employee or contractor who uses the app with their own account.

- The customer whose order is being handled. Some features process their data even though they do not have this app: the order chat, the proof-of-delivery photo and the age check.

This processing is part of the working relationship and of the service the company provides to its customers. That is why the app does not show a consent dialog: knowing which store you are on shift at and who handled each order is what the tool is for. Phone permissions (location, camera and notifications) are requested by Android, and the operator grants or denies them there.

### 2. What data we collect and why

### From the operator

Data What it is used for

Name, email and profile photo Identifying the operator in the app and on its lock screen. The email is the username of their company account.

Password Signing in. The company’s server checks it; the app does not store it. What is stored is the session, encrypted on the phone.

Approximate location Confirming that the operator is at the store when they clock in, when they clock out and while their shift is active. It is approximate: accurate to the block, not to the meter.

Precise location, only when delivering Only for the operator who goes out on deliveries, and only while they have an open delivery stop. It is used to guide them to the customer and to let the customer see where their order is. While it is in use, the phone shows a persistent notification (“Route in progress”). The notification goes away when the last stop is closed.

Device identifier for notifications Sending work alerts to the phone of the operator who is on shift.

Activity log Which operator picked, delivered or took in each order, with date and time. This is the store’s traceability record.

Phone sound status When the operator clocks in and during the shift, the app reports whether notifications are allowed and whether the phone is on silent or “Do Not Disturb.” That way the server knows whether an order alert will make a sound. Nothing else is read from the phone.

Usage and crash data Operational metrics: shifts opened, orders taken, how long picking takes. Also technical reports when the app fails, including a notice when the system force-closed it. Details in section 6.

What you write in “Report a problem” Only if you choose to use it, from Settings: the text you write to tell us about a fault, along with the app version and phone version. It never includes a screenshot.

### From the customer whose order is being handled

Data What it is used for

Name, phone number and delivery address Delivering the order to the right person. The company loads this data from the order; the app only displays it.

Order chat messages and photos Talking with the customer about that order, for example to let them know about a substitution. The chat stays linked to the order.

Proof-of-delivery photo Recording that the order was delivered in full and to the right person.

Photo of the national ID card (cédula), only for orders with liquor Backing up that the operator checked, at delivery, that the person receiving it is of legal age. It is not used for anything else, and only the manager of that store can see it.

ID card photo of the person bringing a return Backing up who handed in the returned product at the counter. Same rule as above: only the manager of that store can see it.

Cash on delivery: amount, payment method, reference and photo of the card terminal receipt When the order is paid on receipt, the delivery driver records that they collected payment. If it was by card, they photograph the card terminal receipt. The app does not process payments: it only records the collection. The amount is calculated by the company’s server, never by the phone.

Age check record Who did it, when, for which order and where (at the counter or at the customer’s door). It meets the company’s responsible alcohol sales policy.

Reading the ID card with the camera. The operator can point the camera at the ID card so the app reads the date of birth instead of typing it in. That image is not stored and never leaves the phone: it is processed on the device itself, and only the result of the check reaches the server. The operator can always check by eye and confirm by hand.

### 3. What the app does NOT do

- It does not access location outside the shift, and it does not request background location.

- It does not ring or send notifications when the operator is clocked out.

- It does not sell data, show ads or build marketing profiles.

- It does not use the phone’s advertising ID. The app does not even ask for permission to read it.

- It does not send the PIN anywhere. It is a local lock, stored encrypted on the phone.

- It does not send screenshots or screen content in crash reports: those screens show ID cards and addresses.

- It does not send customer data to measurement tools. Only internal identifiers and timings are sent, filtered against a closed list.

- It does not copy its data to the phone’s cloud backup or to a new phone. What the app stores is store work, and it stays on that phone.

- It does not read the operator’s contacts, messages, files or photo gallery. To attach a saved photo, it uses the Android picker, which only hands the app the image that was chosen.

### 4. Where the data is stored

The data is stored on the company’s servers, in its management system (Odoo), together with the rest of the information for each order. The app talks to them over HTTPS only.

The operator’s phone keeps the session and the PIN, encrypted in Android’s secure storage (Keystore). It also keeps scans that have not been sent yet and a cache of product images. When the app is uninstalled, Android deletes all of that.

### 5. For how long it is kept

- Shift location: deleted automatically after 30 days. After that, only a count remains: how many times it was measured and how many of those were inside the store, not where the operator was.

- Delivery route: same rule, 30 days, and it deletes itself.

- ID card photo (liquor deliveries and returns): the image is deleted after 90 days. The record that the check was done, who did it and when remains, but the document does not.

- Messages, chat photos and proof-of-delivery photo: kept with the order for as long as the law requires the fiscal and operational records of that order to be kept.

- Payment record and card terminal receipt photo: these are accounting records and are kept for the period Venezuelan law requires for them.

- Age check record: for as long as there is a legal obligation to keep it.

- Activity log: with the order, for the same reason.

- Crash reports: according to the period configured with the provider, which does not exceed 90 days.

- Usage metrics: according to the period configured in Google Analytics, which does not exceed 14 months.

- PIN and session: live only on the phone and are deleted when you sign out or uninstall the app.

### 6. Who it is shared with

Within the company, access is limited to those who need it for their role: the operator handling the order, the manager of that store and the support team if there is a complaint or a return. ID card photos are more restricted: only the store manager can see them, and every time someone opens one, it is logged.

To work, the app uses these providers. They process the data on the company’s behalf and not for their own purposes:

- Google LLC — Firebase Cloud Messaging: delivers work notifications. It receives the phone’s notification identifier and the alert.

- Google LLC — Google Analytics for Firebase: measures operations (shifts, orders, timings), identified by store and without people’s names. It receives an app installation identifier and technical data about the phone.

- Google LLC — Google Maps Navigation SDK: only for the operator who delivers, with an open stop. It guides the route and receives their precise location while navigating.

- Functional Software, Inc. (Sentry), United States: receives technical reports when the app fails. They include the error, the app and Android versions, the store of the shift and the operator’s internal identifier. They never include their name, their email, screenshots or customer data.

- OpenStreetMap Foundation: serves the delivery map tiles when the Google map is not used. Like any web server, it receives the phone’s IP address and the map area being viewed.

Some of these providers process data outside Venezuela, mainly in the United States.

Beyond that, data is only handed to third parties when a competent authority requires it under the law.

The website. This policy is about the app. The zentrix.company website, where you are probably reading it, shows no advertising and only measures visits with Google Analytics if the visitor accepts it in the cookie notice; without that permission it sets no cookies and loads nothing from Google. What is measured and how to withdraw permission is in [Cookies and analytics](https://zentrix.company/en/privacy/#cookies). Like any website, it is served by a hosting provider (GitHub, with Cloudflare in front), which sees the connection’s IP address in order to deliver the page.

### 7. Access, correction and deletion

Anyone whose data passes through Zentrix Work, whether operator or customer, can ask to see, correct or delete their data. To do so, write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company?subject=Data%20request%20%E2%80%94%20Zentrix%20Work) with the subject Data request — Zentrix Work and the details needed to identify you. Operators can also ask their store manager.

Deleting the account. The app does not let you create accounts, so they are not deleted from it either: the company creates and closes them. When an operator asks to close their account, or leaves the company, their access is revoked and their personal data is deleted. Only what the law requires us to keep is retained, such as the record of who dispatched an order that has already been invoiced.

We respond within 30 business days at most. If something cannot be deleted because of a legal, accounting or tax obligation, or because of an open complaint, we tell you why and for how long.

Signing out, forgetting the PIN or uninstalling the app does not delete anything from the server. It only removes the session from the phone. To delete data, use the channel above.

### 8. Minors

Zentrix Work is a work tool for adults (18 or older) hired by the company. It is not directed at minors and does not knowingly collect data from minors as users.

### 9. Security

- All communication with the company’s servers is encrypted (HTTPS/TLS).

- The session is stored encrypted in Android’s secure storage (Keystore).

- The PIN is stored as a hash, never in plain text, and it never leaves the phone.

- On every operation, the server checks who the operator is, which store they are on shift at and which tasks they are allowed to do. What the phone says is not enough.

- An operator’s access can be revoked at any time, for example if they leave the company or lose their phone. The app signs out the next time it is used.

No security measure is absolute, and we keep working to improve ours.

### 10. Changes to this policy

If the data the app handles changes, this page will be updated and the date at the top will change. Important changes will also be announced to operators through the company’s internal channels.

Change note (October 13, 2026). The app was renamed Zentrix Work, the company the operator works for is now referred to generically (“the company”), and this policy moved from work.guuao.com/privacidad.html to zentrix.company/work/privacidad. Nothing changed about what data is handled, why, or who it is shared with. The paragraph about the website was corrected, because the new site does not use analytics.

### 11. Contact

GUUAO LLC [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company)

## [Terms of use — Zentrix Work](https://zentrix.company/en/work/terms/)

The terms of use of the Zentrix Work app for store staff: what it is for, what you agree to when using it, the data involved and who provides the app.

Legal

### Zentrix Work terms of use

Last updated: September 23, 2026.

### 1. What it is and who provides it

Zentrix Work is the internal work tool for the store staff of the company that uses it (“the company” from here on), provided by GUUAO LLC. By using it, you accept these terms. Your employment relationship is governed by your contract and by labor law; these terms only cover the use of the app.

### 2. Who may use it

Only adults who have been given an operator account by the company. The app does not allow sign-ups. The company decides which store and which tasks you can handle, and the server checks this on every operation.

### 3. Your account, your password and your PIN

Your account is personal and non-transferable. Do not share your password or your PIN, and do not let anyone else work with your session: every operation is recorded under your name. If you lose your phone or think someone used your account, tell your manager right away or write to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company).

### 4. Permitted use

- Use the app only for the company tasks you were assigned.

- Customer data (name, phone number, address, photos and ID card) is confidential. Do not copy it, screenshot it, share it or use it outside the order you are handling.

- Do not try to get around the controls of the app or the server, or use the app at a store or for a task that is not yours.

- The age check is done for real, with the person in front of you. Confirming it without checking is a serious offense.

### 5. The server has the final say

The app shows what the company’s system decides. If the server rejects an operation, the app shows you the reason exactly as it arrives and does not work around it. Operations are recorded with the date, the time and the operator who performed them.

### 6. Your phone

The app runs on your personal phone and is built to use as little as possible: it stays silent when you are off shift, uses location only during your shift and keeps the screen on only while a task is open. Permissions are granted from Android and you can revoke them, although some features will not work without them (for example, you cannot check in without location).

### 7. Availability and versions

We do our best to keep the app available, but there may be outages, faults or maintenance. The company may require a minimum version: if your version is blocked, the app tells you, and you need to update it from Google Play to continue.

### 8. Suspension and termination of access

The company may suspend or close your access when your employment relationship ends, if you breach these terms, or to protect the security of customers and data. What happens to your data afterward is explained in the [privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/#c7).

### 9. Intellectual property

The app, its design and its brand belong to GUUAO LLC. We give you permission to use them only while you work with the app and for what is described here.

### 10. Privacy

What data the app uses and why is explained in the [privacy policy](https://zentrix.company/en/work/privacy/), which is part of these terms.

### 11. Liability

The app is provided as a work tool, as is. To the extent permitted by law, GUUAO LLC is not liable for indirect damages arising from faults in the app, the phone or the network. None of this limits the rights labor law gives you.

### 12. Changes

We may update these terms. The version in force is the one published on this page, with its date at the top. Important changes will be announced through the company’s internal channels.

### 13. Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela. We will first try to settle any disagreement amicably, by writing to [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company). If no agreement is reached within 30 calendar days, the dispute will go to the competent courts of Venezuela. Disputes arising from the employment relationship remain governed by Venezuelan labor law.

### 14. Contact

GUUAO LLC [soporte@zentrix.company](mailto:soporte@zentrix.company)

## [Ajustes — Documentación de Zentrix Work](https://zentrix.company/work/docs/ajustes.html)

Los ajustes de Zentrix Work: probar una llamada, vibrar y sonar al trabajar, el flash en la llamada, el tema oscuro o claro y los permisos de la app.

### Ajustes

Toca el engranaje de arriba. Aquí pruebas que la llamada suene y eliges cómo se siente y cómo se ve la app.

Ajustes: lo que suena, lo que se siente y cómo se ve.

### Probar una llamada

«Suena como la de verdad, para saber si la vas a oír.» Se cierra Ajustes y te suena una llamada con la franja «PRUEBA — no es trabajo de verdad». No toca el sistema ni le llega a nadie.

Hazla el primer día, con el teléfono en el bolsillo, donde lo vas a llevar. Si no la oyes, revisa [el sonido](https://zentrix.company/work/docs/permisos.html#silencio).

### Que se sienta

- Vibrar al trabajar — «Un toque si la lectura entró, dos si algo no va.»

- Sonar al trabajar — «Un pip si la lectura entró, otro distinto si algo no va.»

- Alumbrar en la llamada — «El flash parpadea cuando te toca un pedido, por si no lo oyes.» Solo en teléfonos con flash.

Ojo
«La llamada de un pedido suena y vibra aparte: aquí no se apaga.» Estos interruptores son para el escáner, no para la llamada.

### Cómo se ve

- Claro — «Lo recomendado. Se lee bien hasta a pleno sol.» Viene así. Si ya habías elegido otro tema, la app lo respeta.

- Oscuro — «Gasta menos batería y descansa la vista de noche.»

- Como el teléfono — «Sigue el tema que tenga tu Android.»

- Pantalla completa — «Esconde las barras del teléfono: cabe más en pantalla.»

### Permisos y ubicación

Ves cada permiso con «Concedido» o su botón. Debajo, «Tu ubicación en el turno» te dice qué se guardó en tu último latido: tu zona aproximada, nunca la calle exacta, y solo con el turno abierto.

### La app

- Acerca de Zentrix Work: la política de privacidad y, fuera de la tienda de verdad, a qué servidor apunta.

- Fotos sin gastar datos: una foto que ya viste no se vuelve a bajar.

«Lo demás —tiendas, tareas, turno— lo manda el servidor. Si algo está mal, habla con tu encargado.»

## [Recibir una devolución — Documentación de Zentrix Work](https://zentrix.company/work/docs/devoluciones.html)

Cómo se recibe una devolución en Zentrix Work: contar lo que llegó sin pasarse de lo autorizado, la foto obligatoria y la nota si la cuenta no cuadra.

### Recibir una devolución

El cliente trae de vuelta algo que compró. Tu trabajo es contar lo que llegó y dejar la foto. Nada más.

### Recibir no es aprobar

Soporte ya aprobó la devolución antes de que te llegue. Tú no decides si se devuelve el dinero: solo cuentas.

No te equivoques en esto
Si arriba dice «Soporte todavía no la autorizó»: «No recibas el producto.»

Las devoluciones las abres desde la llamada o desde el acceso Devoluciones de la pantalla principal.

Una devolución autorizada: el motivo, lo que escribió el cliente y la cuenta, que arranca en lo autorizado.

### 1. Cuenta lo que te entregaron

Cada línea arranca en la cantidad autorizada, no en cero. Lo normal es que llegue completo y no toques nada.

- Si llegó menos, baja la línea con Uno menos. La app marca «Falta 1».

- No puedes subir por encima de lo autorizado. «De menos sí (anótalo abajo). De más no: soporte aprobó estas cantidades y recibir no es aprobar.»

Si el cliente trae más de lo autorizado, no lo recibas por la app: avísale a tu encargado.

### 2. La foto es obligatoria

Toma al menos una foto de lo que te entregaron. «Es lo único que respalda a la tienda si después no cuadra.»

Si tomas foto de la cédula, «Tómala solo si el cliente está de acuerdo.» Esa foto después solo la ve el encargado de la tienda: si no ves la de un compañero, es normal.

### 3. Si la cuenta no cuadra, escribe qué pasó

Si bajaste una cantidad, el campo «Qué pasó» es obligatorio. Una línea basta: «Trajo una sola, la otra dice que la perdió…». Con la cuenta completa es opcional.

### 4. Registra la recepción

- Toca «Registrar la recepción». «¿Registrar la recepción?» te dice cuántas unidades vas a registrar. «Queda a tu nombre y con la hora, y no se deshace desde el teléfono.»

- Toca «Sí, registrar». Si dudas, Todavía no.

«Todavía no se puede registrar»
Falta algo: la foto, la nota, o hay una cantidad de más. La app te dice cuál. Arréglalo y vuelve a tocar.

Quedó bien si…
Ves «Recepción registrada.» con cuánto recibiste y cuántas fotos. Toca Listo.
